descriptionPlain:
About Commonwealth Fusion Systems: 
 
Commonwealth Fusion Systems is on a mission to deliver the urgent transition to fusion energy.
 
Combining decades of research, top talent, and new technologies, we’re designing and building commercially viable fusion power plants. And we're working with policymakers, suppliers, and many others to build the energy industry of the future.
 
We’re in the best position to make it happen. Since 2018, we’ve raised $4 billion of capital, making us the largest and leading fusion company in the world.
 
Now we’re looking for more thinkers, doers, builders, and makers to join us. People who’ll bring new perspectives, solve tough problems, and thrive as part of a team. 
 
If that’s you and this role fits, we want to hear from you.


Join the power movement as an Accounts Payable Specialist
 
As an Accounts Payable Specialist, you will be responsible for providing accurate, timely accounts payable processing while helping improve how invoices move from receipt to payment. Reporting to the Accounts Payable Supervisor, the AP Specialist will manage a high-volume invoice queue, investigate discrepancies, coordinate resolution with vendors and internal partners, and support month-end close. The role calls for curiosity about why problems occur and practical ideas that reduce repeat issues, delays, and rework. The AP Supervisor remains accountable for team priorities, oversight, and escalation decisions. The AP Specialist owns assigned invoice processing, documentation, and follow-through; coordinates with the responsible buyer, requester, or approver; and escalates unresolved issues with facts and a proposed next step. Payment approvals, purchasing decisions, and accounting policy remain with authorized owners.

As an Accounts Payable Specialist, you will be responsible for providing accurate, timely accounts payable processing while helping improve how invoices move from receipt to payment. Reporting to the Accounts Payable Supervisor, the AP Specialist will manage a high-volume invoice queue, investigate discrepancies, coordinate resolution with vendors and internal partners, and support month-end close. The role calls for curiosity about why problems occur and practical ideas that reduce repeat issues, delays, and rework. The AP Supervisor remains accountable for team priorities, oversight, and escalation decisions. lists.content:
• Invoice processing: Manage roughly 200–300 invoices per week; verify vendor, invoice number, date, amount, entity, PO, and coding using approved guidance; investigate duplicate alerts before processing

  • Matching and controls: Perform two-way and three-way matching; verify receipts, service approvals, payment terms, tax, freight, and exemption support; resolve or escalate discrepancies before payment

  • Exception resolution: Work with Procurement, Receiving, requesters, and vendors to resolve missing receipts, insufficient PO funds, billing errors, and approval delays; track hold reasons, owners, and next action dates

  • Vendor and payment support: Respond professionally to payment inquiries; obtain corrected invoices and credit memos; track credits and refunds; prepare payment support under established approvals and safeguards, including duplicate-payment checks for automatic debits

  • Month-end support: Identify unbilled vendor and contractor costs; provide accrual support and reconcile vendor statements and AP records; coordinate coding questions and close items with Accounting

  • Process improvement: Identify recurring exceptions and their causes; recommend practical fixes; update procedures and support approved workflow improvements, system testing, and cross-training

  • Own the follow-through: Organize the queue by due date and risk, follow up promptly, and close the loop with vendors and internal partners

  • Ask and investigate: Question unclear or inconsistent information, use supporting records to understand the issue, and bring recommendations to the supervisor

  • Collaborate and protect controls: Work constructively across functions, communicate blockers early, handle sensitive information carefully, and preserve required approvals and documentation

• Relevant high-volume accounts payable experience, including two-way and three-way matching, vendor communication, and month-end support
  • ERP experience required
  • Working knowledge of debits and credits, accruals, expense coding, purchase orders, GL accounts, and reconciliations
  • Strong Excel, strong attention to detail, atrong organization, and clear communication
  • Ability to investigate discrepancies, recognize patterns, follow through, and adapt as processes change

• Perform activities such as typing, standing, or sitting for extended periods of time
  • Work in a facility that contains industrial hazards including heat, cold, noise, fumes, strong magnets, lead (Pb), high voltage, high current, pressure systems, and cryogenics

Join the power movement as an Assembly Test Implementation Engineer

This position is overall responsible for the preparation, execution and closure phases of all related SPARC Assembly test activities.

lists.content:
• Transferrable knowledge / skillset to become adept / proficient in all defined specialized test methods from both an engineering and equipment operation perspective – specialized testing includes complexity or hazard introduction for design verification purposes (low voltage, high voltage, high stored energy, etc.)
  • Support planning functions by scouting field assets for test instruction or procedure planning
  • Review and approve test procedures / instructions to ensure understanding of scope and identify & mitigate potential risks within both the engineering and technician teams
  • Collaborate with the technician team to execute a pre-test walkdown of unit or device under test, sensor, adjacent components, subsystems, systems or infrastructure to assess correct scope and hazard recognition when warranted
  • Collaborate with the technician team to execute custom builds of test equipment / features & mock-up testing for training / derisking purposes (pre-functional testing)
  • Develop software proficiency with SPARC Assembly workflow management for all test activities
  • Provide engineering direction when preparatory or execution impedances are encountered via simple or complex troubleshooting - decide between procedural intent and non-intent changes in the field
  • Adhere to the highest standards of safety and ensure that activities taking place are being performed in strict accordance with CFS safety policies and applicable regulatory safety standards
  • Ensure that activities being performed in the field are conducted in accordance with CFS Standards, standards published by regulatory bodies (NFPA, ASME, ASTM, NET, OSHA, NIOSH, etc.) and Industry Best Practices
  • Reinforce test performance standards - pre-job briefs, procedural place keeping, procedural use and adherence, conservative bias, diligent monitoring of critical parameters, correct data capture, attention to detail, etc.
  • Validate preliminary test outcomes - PASS, FAIL, UNCERTAIN with clear and succinct rationale / communication to integrated stakeholders
  • Collaborate with technician team to ensure full demobilization in the field / proper stowage of all inventory items.
  • Formal Test Engineering approval for all required test reports - signature authority
  • Debrief the test engineering team on performance / procedure feedback to leverage lessons learned, prevent error recurrence and optimize flow for ease of technician execution when deemed prudent
  • Occasional accommodation of off-normal work hours to support critical test activities

• BS in Engineering or related field
  • 5 Years of equivalent engineering experience
  • Previous testing experience with hazards
  • Previous electrical testing experience (high voltage)
  • High proficiency MS Office, Bluebeam or Acrobat, and 3D modeling programs

• OSHA 10
  • NFPA 70E

• Ability to occasionally lift up to 50 lbs
  • Perform activities such as typing, standing, stooping, climbing or sitting for extended periods of time
  • Required onsite 5 days/week when assembly operations with relevant tools are underway, with possible alternating first or second shift assignment
  • Work in a facility that contains industrial hazards including heat, cold, noise, fumes, strong magnets, lead (Pb), high voltage, high current, pressure systems, and cryogenics

This role is a true n of 1: you will be the company's dedicated commercial legal lead, operating as both a hands-on individual contributor on CFS's most complex, mission-critical transactions and the architect of the legal infrastructure that will support the company's next phase of commercial growth. Join the power movement as Assistant General Counsel – Commercial

CFS is seeking an experienced, pragmatic, and highly strategic Assistant General Counsel – Commercial to serve as a foundational leader on our legal team. This is a rare opportunity to shape how legal operates at a company building an entirely new industry from the ground up.

This role is a true n of 1: you will be the company's dedicated commercial legal lead, operating as both a hands-on individual contributor on CFS's most complex, mission-critical transactions and the architect of the legal infrastructure that will support the company's next phase of commercial growth. As CFS scales, you will be expected to build and lead a team in commercial and corporate legal, making this as much a leadership opportunity as a technical legal one.

Reporting directly to the Chief Legal Officer, you will partner with executive leaders across commercial and business development, corporate development, strategic partnerships, supply chain, finance, and engineering — giving you direct visibility into, and influence over, the company's most consequential strategic decisions

lists.content: CFS is at an inflection point, moving from R&D to commercial execution. The deals, structures, and legal foundation this person builds now will directly shape how CFS contracts, partners, and scales for years to come. This is not a maintenance role — it is a builder role, for someone who wants outsized ownership over both the substance of high-stakes deals and the systems that make the whole commercial legal function work.

Build & Scale the Commercial Legal Function Serve as the architect of CFS's commercial legal capability — building on and improving existing processes to create scalable contract workflows, tools, standard templates, negotiation playbooks, and training that empower business teams and accelerate deal velocity. Lay the groundwork for, and ultimately recruit and lead, a team as the function grows

Lead High-Stakes Commercial and Partnership Negotiations Structure, draft, and negotiate complex, high-value commercial and partnership agreements, including key customer, supplier, and vendor deals, long-term procurement contracts, joint developments, strategic alliances, and partnerships

Drive Corporate Development & Strategic Partnerships Serve as a core legal partner on corporate development initiatives — strategic partnerships, joint ventures, strategic investments, technology transfers, licensing, and other complex transactions central to scaling commercial fusion. Partner closely with corporate development and open innovation teams to structure and close deals that advance CFS's strategic position

Support Core Corporate Legal Matters Provide legal support on corporate, subsidiary and entity management, and corporate transactions as they relate to commercial, corporate development, or strategic partnership transactions and agreements, serving as a trusted resource to the CLO, CFO, and CCO on corporate-adjacent legal needs beyond commercial deal work

Advise Supply Chain & Operations Serve as the primary legal advisor to procurement and global supply chain teams, mitigating risk across complex, multi-tiered international supply chains for advanced hardware, specialized materials, and manufacturing

Drive Pragmatic Risk Management Provide business-minded, creative, and actionable legal guidance that balances risk mitigation with the urgency and agility required to hit CFS's commercial milestones

Cross-Functional Leadership & Collaboration Partner closely with commercial, corporate development, supply chain, engineering, global affairs, finance, and compliance teams to ensure alignment and seamless execution across all commercial and corporate development activity — and act as a visible legal leader within the broader organization

Education & Bar: J.D. from an accredited law school and active bar admission in good standing in at least one U.S. jurisdiction (eligible for MA In-House Counsel registration)
 
Experience: 12+ years of legal experience, ideally starting at a top-tier law firm followed by significant in-house experience at a fast-growing, complex technology, energy, advanced manufacturing, or industrial company
 
Commercial Expertise: Deep background in drafting and negotiating complex commercial contracts, strategic partnerships, global supply chain agreements, and corporate development transactions (JVs, strategic investments, licensing, tech transfer)
 
Corporate Legal Exposure: Familiarity with core corporate legal matters — governance, entity structuring, and general corporate transaction support — sufficient to advise confidently alongside commercial work
 
0-to-1 Process Builder: Proven track record of creating, operationalizing, and/or improving commercial legal systems, contract management tools (CLM), and negotiation playbooks from the ground up
 
Leadership Trajectory: Experience mentoring, managing, or building legal teams, or a clear readiness to do so — this role is expected to grow into a team lead position
 
Business Acumen & Pragmatism: Exceptional judgment and the ability to synthesize complex technical, operational, and legal concepts into clear, actionable advice for non-lawyers
 
Executive Presence: Comfort advising senior leadership and acting as a trusted strategic partner to the CLO and business unit executives
 
Adaptability & Drive: A proactive, self-starter mentality comfortable operating in a fast-changing, high-ambiguity environment where innovation happens daily
 
Mission Alignment: A genuine passion for clean energy, deep technology, science-based product commercialization, and CFS's mission to bring fusion to the grid

• Dedication to safety to mitigate hazards that may include heat, cold, noise, fumes, strong magnets, lead, high voltage, and cryogenics
  • Willingness to occasionally travel or work required nights/weekends/on-call

About Commonwealth Fusion Systems: 
 
Commonwealth Fusion Systems is on a mission to deliver the urgent transition to fusion energy.
 
Combining decades of research, top talent, and new technologies, we’re designing and building commercially viable fusion power plants. And we're working with policymakers, suppliers, and many others to build the energy industry of the future.
 
We’re in the best position to make it happen. Since 2018, we’ve raised $4 billion of capital, making us the largest and leading fusion company in the world.
 
Now we’re looking for more thinkers, doers, builders, and makers to join us. People who’ll bring new perspectives, solve tough problems, and thrive as part of a team. 
 
If that’s you and this role fits, we want to hear from you.


Join the power movement as a Control Software Engineer 
 
As a Control Software Engineer, you will be responsible for the design, implementation, and verification of software and controls for advanced R&D equipment and complex machinery.
 
As a member of the Software Engineering team you will be a hands-on technical contributor, a champion of writing excellent quality, production-ready code for mission-critical real-time systems. You will collect functional requirements from customers and produce software solutions to meet these requirements.
 
You will work with a variety of engineers to integrate your software into software testbeds, hardware testbeds, and the production tools.  You will also contribute to the broader software ecosystem to improve tooling and processes used across the company.

lists.content:
• Develop control software across multiple platforms, including PLCs and real-time Linux
  • Develop operator interfaces and workflows
  • Improve software tooling to increase developer velocity and enable new capabilities

• Bachelor's degree in a relevant engineering field (computer science, computer engineering, electrical engineering, industrial engineering, etc.)
  • 5+ years of experience with industrial control systems and/or embedded control systems
  • 5+ years of experience in producing production quality control software
  • Experience with modern software development lifecycle practices (CI/CD, git version control, unit testing, integration testing, etc)
  • Proficiency with Python
  • Proficiency with at least one real-time control language (C++, SCL/ST, Rust, etc)

• Experience with industrial protocols (e.g. EtherCat, Profinet, Modbus, etc)
  • Experience developing Human-Machine Interfaces (HMIs) for industrial or scientific equipment
  • Familiarity with industrial control platforms (e.g. Beckhoff or TwinCat)
  • Familiarity with Linux
  • Familiarity with general networking (IP/UDP)

• Perform activities such as typing, standing, sitting, etc. for extended periods of time
  • Dedication to safety to mitigate industrial hazards that may include heat, cold, noise, fumes, strong magnets, lead (Pb), high voltage, high current, pressure systems, and cryogenics
  • Willingness to occasionally travel or work required nights/weekends/on-call

Join the power movement as a Controls Engineer

As a Controls Engineer, you are proficient in most or all core functions of your discipline, executing mid-to-long term assignments that are loosely defined. You operate with general guidance from management, increasingly taking independent ownership of developing execution approaches for equipment and process concepts.

You will generate work plans and define milestones for your own tasks, identifying and mitigating lower-risk items. You will provide technical leadership on short-term problems within your group's scope and lead formal design reviews with cross-functional teams.

lists.content:
• Independently own the complete lifecycle — physical mounting, pneumatic/electrical integration, and PLC I/O mapping through commissioning — for smaller equipment components and upgrades, handing off to Manufacturing Engineering
  • Support production equipment on the floor — troubleshoot faults, restore uptime, and follow through with root-cause analysis and preventative fixes
  • Provide technical leadership on short-term problems within your group's scope; lead formal design reviews with cross-functional teams (equipment/MEs)
  • Contribute to system architectures and electrical schematics, applying and standardizing elements compliant with NFPA79/NEC/UL508A standards
  • Write and debug PLC structured text with an emphasis on code that is organized, documented, maintainable, and reusable
  • Contribute to department policies, tool development, and the characterization of automated processes using data-driven approaches like Cpk and Gage R&R
  • Respectfully raise concerns and share data-driven perspectives in group settings to support the best path forward
  • Identify and mitigate lower-risk items (e.g., lead times, part tolerances) by coordinating with standard vendors; escalate larger risks to management

• Bachelor’s degree in engineering field is required
  • 4+ years' experience as controls engineer on electro-mechanical systems
  • Proficiency in Structured Text and Ladder; working knowledge of other IEC 61131-3 languages
  • Ability to apply sound reasoning and judgment on tasks and near-term project decisions, with review and support from senior engineers
  • Working knowledge of control-related safety systems (ANSI/RIA15.06/OSHA compliant) and enclosure design compliant with NFPA79/NEC/UL508A standards
  • A reliable and persistent work ethic, seeing tasks through to completion and staying determined in the face of uncertainty and failure
  • Familiarity with manufacturing equipment and hands-on fabrication or assembly skills (e.g., rotating machinery, cable winding, soldering, pipe bending, or similar)
  • Collaboration experience with job shops and external vendors
  • High self-motivation and drive to execute quickly with strong troubleshooting and problem-solving skills
  • A value for design for manufacturability, serviceability, and simplicity over complexity

• Experience in Beckhoff and Siemens controls platforms
  • Experience in Ignition SCADA systems
  • Experience integrating equipment data into SCADA/data systems (e.g., IO-Link, MQTT)
  • Machine Vision experience
  • Greenfield or brownfield startup commissioning experience
  • Expertise with CAD drafting, specifically AutoCAD Electrical

• Ability to lift up to 50 lbs occasionally
  • Perform activities such as typing, standing, stooping, and sitting, for extended periods of time
  • Dedication to safety to mitigate hazards that may include heat, cold, noise, fumes, strong magnets, lead, high voltage, and cryogenics
  • Willingness to occasionally travel or work required nights/weekends/on-call

Join the power movement as CSA Project Engineer  

Responsible for activities relating to design and construction engineering within the civil, structural, and architectural (CSA) discipline, but is also familiar with other construction disciplines. Duties include working with engineering teams in the planning, sequencing, assembling, and issuing of Construction Work Packages; development of installation specifications, 3D model coordination, interpreting design drawings and specifications, field verification of materials, monitoring construction progress, response to questions by constructors, providing direction in the field to ensure construction is in compliance with engineering documentation and developing turnover packages to commissioning.

lists.content:
• Collaborate with engineering to address constructability and design issues relating to civil, structural, and architectural scopes for process systems
  • Provide review and approval of external civil, structural, or architectural engineering documentation and specifications 
  • Interface with outside engineering firms for CSA designs
  • Lead cross functional 3D model reviews to identify constructability, installation, and resolve interface issues
  • Identify the content of engineering document packages (Work Packages) required to support construction activities in the field
  • Plan, sequence, assemble, and issue Construction Work Packages
  • Partner with engineering teams responsible for process systems to facilitate efficient conversion of design deliverables into construction ready work
  • Oversee the maintenance of construction configuration management
  • Work with Contractor to support tracking, reporting, and forecasting activities in the field
  • Coordinate with the Procurement Organization for field procured materials, material substitution, services, and equipment
  • Review material receiving reports and warehousing to assure delivery of correct materials
  • Coordinate the preparation of cost reports, forecasts, and progress reports
  • Coordinate with Field Supervision and Subcontractors to plan/support construction schedules
  • Recommend and implement procedures to ensure construction remains in compliance with the requirements of engineering and design
  • Ensure engineering and procurement provide timely delivery of drawings, materials, and equipment
  • Support the construction quality program
  • Support problem solving in the field and serve as liaison between Construction and Engineering
  • Support development and implementation of the Request for Information (RFI)/Field Change Request (FCR) process between Construction and CFS engineering
  • Manage system turnover schedule with construction managing contractor
  • Develop turnover packages in accordance with defined system / sub-system breakdown
  • Track pending issues and actions impacting system turnover
  • Coordinate and facilitate system walkdowns
  • Review field generated inspection records for quality and completeness
  • Review field generated punch list items for quality and completeness and progress in project database
  • Support the implementation of the records retention and turnover plans

• BS in Civil Engineering, Structural Engineering, or related engineering discipline
  • Minimum of 5 years supporting design, construction, and execution of civil/structural projects or process systems with structural requirements 
  • Demonstrated understanding of the engineering, design, and construction lifecycle for complex industrial facilities or process systems
  • Experience supporting civil, structural, and architectural (CSA) scopes, including structural steel, concrete, foundations, embeds, anchors, equipment supports, and building systems
  • Codes and standards with additional knowledge of IBC, AISC, ACI, and ASCE
  • Ability to read and understand engineering documents issued for construction such as P&IDs and isometric drawings
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced construction environment

• Codes and standards with additional knowledge of IBC, AISC, ACI, and ASCE

• Perform activities such as stooping, climbing, typing, standing, or sitting for extended periods of time
  • Dedication to safety to mitigate industrial hazards that may include heat, cold, noise, fumes, strong magnets, lead (Pb), high voltage, and cryogenics
  • Willingness to travel or work required nights/weekends/on-call occasionally

descriptionPlain:
About Commonwealth Fusion Systems: 
 
Commonwealth Fusion Systems is on a mission to deliver the urgent transition to fusion energy.
 
Combining decades of research, top talent, and new technologies, we’re designing and building commercially viable fusion power plants. And we're working with policymakers, suppliers, and many others to build the energy industry of the future.
 
We’re in the best position to make it happen. Since 2018, we’ve raised $4 billion of capital, making us the largest and leading fusion company in the world.
 
Now we’re looking for more thinkers, doers, builders, and makers to join us. People who’ll bring new perspectives, solve tough problems, and thrive as part of a team. 
 
If that’s you and this role fits, we want to hear from you.


Join the power movement as a Diagnostics Mechanical Engineer
Commonwealth Fusion Systems is assembling the high-field SPARC tokamak, which aims to be the first magnetic fusion device to achieve net fusion energy, and is predicted to be able to achieve high gain and fusion power up to 140 MW.  We are completing the design and have begun the assembly and installation of diagnostic systems that will be used to control the plasma and deliver the scientific data necessary to complete the design of ARC. These include approximately 40 sub-systems covering magnetics, interferometry, neutral pressure, x-ray to visible spectroscopy, camera imaging, bolometry, neutrons, Thomson scattering, electron cyclotron emission, reflectometry, Langmuir probes and structural temperature and strain sensing.  A more detailed overview can be found at: https://pubs.aip.org/aip/rsi/article/95/10/103518/3317155.
 CFS is looking to grow the SPARC team in order to complete the mechanical design and integration of these diagnostic systems as they move through design closeout, analysis, procurement, test, and installation. At present we’re finalizing the design and starting assembly for many of the front-end, in vacuum measurement devices and are looking to add multi-faceted support to help carry those designs across the finish line, take on engineering challenges associated with their build and test, and help design the structural components associated with ex-vessel data transmission to our diagnostic labs. Candidates will work as part of an integrated diagnostic team along with fusion scientists and other engineers to demonstrate net energy from a tokamak for the first time. CFS encourages applications from both senior and early career engineers and those interested in cross-industry career changes to help us build a diverse team to meet our mission goals.

lists.content:
• Shepherd SPARC diagnostic sub-systems through design closeout, test, and procurement, working with a team of scientists, designers, analysts and engineers
  • Integrate technical input from experts on the team to ensure diagnostic designs will survive SPARC’s harsh environments and be usable to achieve SPARC’s scientific mission goals
  • Coordinate with manufacturing engineers to align on build and test strategy for complex integrated systems, and support builds in the field to maintain quality and speed
  • Contribute to a strong safety culture

• Bachelor’s degree in a relevant engineering field (mechanical, aerospace, civil or nuclear)
  • 5+ years of relevant experience designing and delivering mechanical systems
  • Demonstrated examples of delivering cradle-to-grave mechanical design with nuanced environmental or performance requirements
  • Experience designing for manufacturing and assembly, and collaborating with partners to oversee or carry out integrated builds
  • Bias toward action, and a balance of engineering intuition and technical rigor that allows for robust, simple designs to be generated with speed
  • First principles based approach to engineering and ability to understand concepts and tradeoffs that bridge engineering and physics
  • Strong communication skills to gather inputs and distribute information across several partner teams

• Experience with Siemens NX, Teamcenter, or Ansys as CAD, PLM, and analysis tools
  • Experience with software development, particularly in Python
  • Experience designing large equipment requiring lifting/rigging tools to assemble
  • Experience with design of systems for exposure to high stress, UHV, high temperature, high magnetic field, and/or radiation environments

• Ability to occasionally lift up to 50 lbs
  • Perform activities such as climbing, typing, standing, or sitting for extended periods of time
  • Willingness to travel or work required nights/weekends/on-call occasionally
  • Work in a facility that contains industrial hazards including heat, cold, noise, fumes, strong magnets, lead (Pb), high voltage, high current, pressure systems, and cryogenics

We are seeking a strategic and analytical Director of Manufacturing, Operations & Supply Chain Finance to lead our operations finance team.

Join the power movement as Director, Corporate FP&A

We are seeking a strategic and analytical Director, Corporate FP&A, to drive our enterprise-level financial planning processes. This role sits at the center of how the company sets direction, allocates capital, and measures performance—translating complex financial and operational data into the insights that guide Executive Leadership and Board decisions. The Director will partner across Finance, including Accounting and Investor Relations, to ensure a consistent, credible financial narrative and help mature the infrastructure to enable scale.

lists.content:
Planning Process & Risk Governance:

  • Oversee corporate planning cycles and direct the financial planning calendar, cadence and interconnectivity including the budgets, forecasts and long-range plans
  • Establish standards, timelines, and governance that keep the planning process disciplined and on schedule
  • Evaluate effectiveness of the planning and reporting processes with a view to continuous improvement
  • Maintain the enterprise financial risk register, tracking key risks, mitigation actions, and surfacing material exposures

    • Strategic Planning & Decision Support:

    • Lead the cadence and guide preparation of Executive Committee and Board reporting packages, ensuring materials are accurate and insight-driven. Distill complex analysis into clear narratives and recommendations for senior stakeholders
    • Own enterprise cash forecasting, providing visibility into liquidity, working capital, and cash flow to support capital deployment and funding decisions
    • Support enterprise capital allocation evaluations, target setting, financial modeling, and scenario analysis

      • Team Leadership, Partnership & Transformation:

      • Oversee a shared pool of financial analysts supporting the broader finance team, ensuring consistent quality and effective coverage across the organization
      • Serve as a financial advisor to the G&A and R&D leadership teams to drive capital allocation decisions or development of business cases as needed
      • Partner with Accounting and Investor Relations on financial results narratives, ensuring alignment across stakeholder needs
      • Collaborate with the Finance Systems lead, IT, and other cross-functional teams on maintenance of financial planning tools and reporting integrations with other systems. Support Global Finance transformation, including AI adoption and process improvements, to enhance the speed, quality, and scalability of the FP&A function

• Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field; MBA, CPA, or CFA preferred
  • 15+ years of progressive finance experience, with significant time in corporate FP&A, strategic finance, or a comparable function
  • Demonstrated experience and executive-level communication and storytelling in preparing materials for Company leadership and Boards
  • Advanced financial modeling and scenario analysis expertise; deep command of enterprise planning processes

• Familiarity with modern FP&A tooling and interest in applying AI and automation to finance workflows
  • Experience supporting a high-growth company

• Perform activities such as typing, standing, or sitting for extended periods of time
  • Willingness to travel or work required nights/weekends/on-call occasionally
  • Work in a facility that contains industrial hazards including heat, cold, noise, fumes, strong magnets, lead (Pb), high voltage, high current, pressure systems, and cryogenics

Join the power movement as Director, Manufacturing, Operations & Supply Chain Finance

We are seeking a strategic and analytical Director of Manufacturing, Operations & Supply Chain Finance to lead our operations finance team.

The ideal candidate blends deep Manufacturing and Operations Finance expertise with the executive presence needed to influence operational strategy and manage manufacturing costs. Reporting to the VP FP&A, this role provides financial leadership across manufacturing sites, including planning, reporting, inventory management, capital investment, and continuous improvement initiatives.

The Director of Manufacturing, Operations & Supply Chain Finance will manage a team of finance business partners, owning finance support across the plants/BUs, and allocations across a matrixed Operations team. As CFS shifts from proving fusion to manufacturing it, this key role will build the operations-finance leadership that turns the breakthrough into economics that support scalability.

lists.content:
• Hire, train, support, develop and coach the members of the team
  • Define, assign and monitor objectives
  • Have management responsibility for meeting cost, quality and delivery objectives for SPARC DDR, FTL and other assigned projects
  • In close coordination with the engineering and construction leaders, plan and assign work, manage the workload and define priorities
  • Act as an escalation point to solve issues
  • Own relationships at executive level with major suppliers
  • Ensure process adherence and improvements for strategic sourcing, purchase orders placement/management and supplier quality
  • Report on project status, risks and issues to the supply chain and project leadership teams
  • Lead the execution of business transformation initiatives

• Bachelor’s degree in supply chain, engineering, business, finance or other related fields
  • 10+ years’ related work experience in supply chain in highly technical environment
  • 10+ years’ successful experience managing and developing a team
  • Previous experience sourcing and overseeing complex projects, including equipment, parts and services spanning across multiple commodities
  • Experience in a startup environment
  • Ability to communicate with all functions, at all levels, internally and externally
  • Ability to structure and negotiate complex contracts
  • Ability to develop sourcing strategies for projects or commodities
  • Ability to earn trust, maintain positive and professional relationships, and strengthen our culture of inclusion.
  • Organizational and project management skills
  • Customer service mindset and entrepreneurial spirit
  • Exceptional creative problem solving and critical thinking skills
  • Demonstrate integrity, respect, attention to detail, collaboration, creativity and agility
  • Ability to work well under pressure in a dynamic environment

• Master’s degree in the field of Supply Chain, Engineering, Business, Finance or other related field 
  • Experience managing a team of people leaders
  • Experience implementing a Supplier Development function
  • Successful experience leading a business transformation project

• Perform activities such as typing, standing, or sitting for extended periods of time
  • Willingness to travel or work required nights/weekends/on-call occasionally for travel to construction sites and supplier
  • Work in a facility that contains industrial hazards including heat, cold, noise, fumes, strong magnets, lead (Pb), high voltage, high current, pressure systems, and cryogenics

Join the power movement as an Electrical Engineer 

Electrical Engineer reporting to the Manager of Power System Team in the Electrical Power Distribution System (EPDS) team at CFS. Responsible for assisting and lead the coordinate electrical design projects and interface with cross-function stakeholders while ensuring a high-quality execution of design release that meets specifications and project timelines.

lists.content:
• Execute installation and testing of complex high power electrical systems for SPARC’s pulsed and steady state power system
  • Develop technical requirements for vendor electrical equipment based on simulations and analysis of the SPARC power system
  • Develop and implement test methods and test plans to qualify newly developed electrical designs
  • Lead the installation, test, and operations handover for electrical designs
  • Lead electrical work package releases (equipment list, drawings, schematics)
  • Apply core electrical engineering knowledge and experience to design and improve high power systems (including but not limited to switchgear, transformers, switchboards, panelboards, reactors, semiconductor devices, cooling systems and control systems)
  • Develop control narratives, concept of operations, and commissioning procedures for newly developed electrical systems
  • Interface with SPARC cross functional teams including R&D, physics, construction, manufacturing, software, test, compliance & commissioning, etc. to ensure all requirements are met
  • Support vendor coordination and quote procurement
  • Apply best electrical safety practices & compliance standards in design and implementation
  • Work on advanced development to develop in-house electrical power technologies for the future of CFS

• 5+ years of related experience with bachelor’s degree (or) a master’s degree with 2+ years of experience with electrical distribution systems or battery based systems
  • Ability to work with a technical team from conception of ideas through implementation in a fast-paced environment
  • Proven experience working on a team while also contributing technically to engineering projects
  • Experience in design and implementation of power systems in the electrical power industry
  • Experience with Medium Voltage & Low Voltage systems (AC/DC power distribution, power conversion, energy storage solutions)
  • Experience with modeling, simulation and analysis backed with validation via functional testing
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, ability to conduct design reviews, organize and present results to both expert and non-technical audiences
  • Results driven and ability to embrace and convince stakeholders of a change in design direction in pursuit of a high-quality product release
  • Familiarity with the National Electric Code & IEEE standards for 3ph power systems
  • Experience with writing technical specifications for electrical equipment
  • The candidate should specialize in electrical system execution in a construction setting

• Experience in practical application of electrical engineering skills to construction, manufacturing, testing and field installations
  • Experience with energy storage (batteries, capacitors etc.)
  • Experience in problem solving, root cause analysis and field containment actions
  • Experience with hands on prototype build, prototype testing and documentation of results.
  • Experience with MFiles, NX (2D and 3D), Teamcenter
  • Experience with ETAP, SKM, and/or Easypower and protective relay programming (acSELerator)
  • Experience with AutoCAD and/or Aveva Electrical, NX(2D and 3D),  Bluebeam, and creation of electrical design drawings such as Single Lines, Panel Schedules and Electrical Schematic Diagrams
  • Experience with grounding, bonding and lightning protection design
  • Experience with AC industrial power distribution design, including emergency power backup systems like emergency diesel generators and uninterruptible power supplies

• Ability to lift up to 50lbs
  • Perform activities such as standing, typing or sitting for extended periods of time
  • Willingness to travel or work required nights/weekends/on-call occasionally
  • Work in a facility that contains industrial hazards including heat, cold, noise, fumes, strong magnets, lead (Pb), high voltage, high current, pressure systems, and cryogenics

lists.content:
• Serve as the primary technical point of contact for end-user support across enterprise applications, resolving user tickets and performing root-cause analysis to identify and implement solutions
  • Manage user onboarding, offboarding, group assignments, and role-based access control across core platforms
  • Execute routine technical updates and application maintenance, including modifying workflows, updating UI elements, and editing system configurations
  • Author, update, and maintain clear documentation, standard operating procedures, and technical guides to streamline knowledge sharing
  • Deliver practical training sessions to onboard new users and educate existing users on best practices and new features
  • Audit software license usage to optimize provisioning, while automating routine administrative tasks and reporting
  • Assist in user acceptance testing and system validation for new releases, patch updates, and custom feature rollouts
  • Monitor and troubleshoot digital thread connections and data flows between enterprise systems

• Bachelor’s degree, preferably in Engineering, Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related STEM field (or equivalent industry experience)
  • Proven ability to troubleshoot complex issues, diagnose root causes, and follow logical steps to resolve technical problems
  • Strong commitment to end-user support, with patience, empathy, and enthusiasm for helping internal stakeholders solve daily challenges
  • Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with a proven ability to explain technical solutions to non-technical stakeholders
  • Core software literacy, including a grasp of conditional logic, basic programming concepts, and data flows across connected systems
  • Meticulous attention to detail, ensuring system changes are applied safely and documentation is thorough, clear, and reliable
  • Fast learner with high curiosity and strong growth potential, energized by complex problem solving in a dynamic environment
  • Deep alignment with our mission to deliver the urgent transition to fusion energy, paired with a genuine passion for solving hard problems

• Familiarity with enterprise software platforms, including Teamcenter (PLM), Designcenter/NX (CAD), Odoo (ERP), Manufacturo/Opcenter (MES), and AVEVA
  • Basic understanding of engineering, manufacturing, and assembly processes in a technical environment
  • Practical experience writing scripts or database queries (Python, PowerShell, SQL) for task automation or data manipulation
  • Working knowledge of web technologies and stylesheets (XML, HTML, CSS) or low-code application development platforms (Mendix)
  • Practical experience using Jira for project/task tracking and Confluence for knowledge base documentation
  • Previous experience in a technical support, IT service desk, or systems administration role

• Perform activities such as typing, standing, and sitting, for extended periods of time
  • Willingness to occasionally travel or work required nights/weekends/on-call 
  • Work in a facility that contains industrial hazards including heat, cold, noise, fumes, strong magnets, lead (Pb), high voltage, high current, pressure systems, and cryogenics

Join the power movement as an Environmental Health & Safety Technician
 
The Environmental Health & Safety Technician plays a dynamic, hands-on role in supporting the Devens-campus EHS team and driving day-to-day operational excellence across the campus. This position conducts continuous field process confirmations, routine building inspections, equipment verifications, and swift corrective action resolution across multiple campus facilities. Additionally, this role provides flexible operational support across environmental programs, leading or assisting with compliance tasks as operational needs evolve.

lists.content:
Field Inspections, Corrective Actions & General EHS
  • Conduct frequent floor walks and field process confirmations across campus buildings to verify safe work practices and operating conditions
  • Facilitate regular safety audits and inspections on walking-working surfaces, ladders, tools, and operational areas using standardized checklists
  • Identify workplace hazards and unsafe conditions immediately, initiating prompt corrective actions and ensuring timely follow-up to closure
  • Respond flexibly to ad-hoc EHS requests, urgent floor issues, special projects, and dynamic campus needs
  • Assist EHS Specialists with incident, injury, and near-miss investigations, including root cause analysis and preventative action tracking
  • Support industrial hygiene monitoring and employee exposure assessments across facilities
  • Help roll out and maintain site-specific safety programs, safe work practices, and job hazard analyses (JHAs).

    • Safety & Emergency Equipment Management

  • Inspect, test, and coordinate routine servicing for campus life safety equipment, including fire extinguishers, fall protection gear, first aid kits, AEDs, safety showers, and eyewash stations
  • Verify that lifting and rigging equipment across all areas is inspected and maintained per regulations and manufacturer standards
  • Calibrate and maintain fixed and portable gas detection equipment according to scheduled intervals.

    • Environmental Program Support & Compliance

  • Perform weekly inspections of hazardous material and hazardous waste storage areas, including satellite accumulation areas across buildings and central storage sites
  • Ensure all waste streams (hazardous, universal, waste oil, and recyclables) are properly labeled, segregated, and stored
  • Maintain accurate compliance logs, including waste drum logs, sign-in sheets, and VOC/solvent usage tracking
  • Conduct weekly campus stormwater inspections in accordance with the SWPPP
  • Assist waste disposal contractors during waste staging, loading, and shipment processes
  • Perform spill prevention tasks, maintain campus spill response kits, and assist with implementing the SPCC plan
  • Assist with internal environmental compliance assessments and due diligence reviews

• High school diploma or equivalency certificate
  • 6+ years of experience implementing and overseeing aspects related to an environmental, health and safety program
  • Previous experience in a construction/industrial environment
  • Ability to work in a high-volume, fast paced environment
  • Required experience in performing safety oversight in an industrial environment
  • Requirement of knowledge of regulatory requirements from agencies like OSHA, EPA, DEC, RCRA, and others

• Experience in managing hazardous waste storage and satellite accumulation areas
  • Experience implementing/developing health and safety plans and programs
  • Experience with emergency response incidents involving hazardous and non-hazardous material releases to air, soil, and water
  • Demonstrated strong propensity for hands-on work and attention to detail in either academic or career pursuits
  • Ability to multitask, to manage shifting priorities and to follow through on projects with minimal supervision
  • Strong organizational and communication skills

• Ability to occasionally lift up to 50 lbs
  • Perform activities such as stooping, climbing, typing, standing, or sitting for extended periods of time
  • Dedication to safety to mitigate industrial hazards that may include heat, cold, noise, fumes, strong magnets, lead (Pb), high voltage, and cryogenics
  • Willingness to occasionally travel or work required nights/weekends/on-call

lists.content:
• Assemble, operate, and maintain custom equipment used in the HTS and characterization lab
  • Perform mechanical and electrical troubleshooting across vacuum, thermal, and instrumentation systems
  • Support equipment integration, testing, and commissioning efforts in collaboration with engineers and vendors
  • Conduct preventive maintenance and servicing of roughing pumps, turbo pumps, cryopumps, and deposition chambers
  • Perform helium leak detection and support vacuum system upgrades, chamber modifications, and process hardware installations
  • Fabricate and repair cable harnesses, sensors, and custom fixturing
  • Use diagnostic tools (multimeters, vacuum gauges, RGA) to troubleshoot systems and support data collection
  • Maintain infrastructure, documentation, and compliance with safety protocols, SOPs, and industry standards (SEMI, OSHA)
  • Contribute to lab cleanliness, organization, and continuous process improvements

• 5+ years of hands-on experience supporting semiconductor, R&D, or manufacturing equipment
  • Strong background in vacuum systems (HV/UHV) including chamber assembly, component cleaning, and leak testing
  • Experience operating or maintaining thin-film deposition tools such as sputtering or evaporation systems
  • Skilled in servicing and refurbishing vacuum pumps (scroll, turbo, cryo)
  • Working knowledge of low- and high-voltage electrical systems, cable harness fabrication, and system wiring
  • Ability to troubleshoot electrical and instrumentation systems using bench tools and diagnostics equipment
  • Understanding of safety protocols including OSHA, LOTO, and PPE use in lab environments
  • Strong safety-first mindset and attention to detail in high-hazard environments

• Experience in pilot-line or production environments with thin-film deposition equipment
  • Knowledge of cryogenics, thermal control systems, and process gas delivery
  • Familiarity with SEMI equipment standards and maintenance tracking tools (CMMS, lab management software).
  • Basic CAD skills for reviewing and modifying mechanical and electrical designs

• Ability to occasionally lift up to 50 lbs
  • Perform activities such as stooping, climbing, standing, or sitting for extended periods of time
  • Dedication to safety to mitigate industrial hazards that may include heat, cold, noise, fumes, strong magnets, lead (Pb), high voltage, and cryogenics
  • Willingness to travel or work required nights/weekends/on-call occasionally

Join the power movement as a Fiber Optic Specialist
 
The Fiber Optic Applications Technician is an exciting and evolving role with a responsibility for assisting R&D and production staff with all aspects of optical fiber work such as fiber splicing, testing, and incorporation of fibers into complex design features while minimizing damage and attenuation to the fiber throughout its lifetime. The technician will ensure functional operation and preventative maintenance of equipment as well as continuous improvement. Responsibilities include close cooperation with Operations, Maintenance, Quality and other departments to ensure goals and objectives are met. lists.content:
• Conduct the handling, routing, splicing, testing, and potential repair of 1000’s of fibers throughout the SPARC fusion machine
  • Perform mechanical integration of small assemblies adjacent or in conjunction with the fiber work, such as passthrough flanges and enclosures for the fibers
  • Install composite or polymer wrappings for the fibers and their enclosures
  • Train other technicians as needed in the proper installation, splicing, routing, and measurement procedures
  • Improve safety protocols for laser and fiber optic handling
  • Fulfill manufacturing and R&D fiber needs

• 4+ years experience in fiber optics field applications
  • Experience with taking attenuation, insertion loss, and spectral analysis measurements using various measurement equipment (such as OTDR, OSA, OBR, power meter, etc.)
  • Must have experience fiber handling in a lab setting with known standards

• 7+ years experience in fiber optics field applications
  • Experience in utilizing distributed sensing arrays
  • Experience with polyimide and a variety of coated fibers
  • At least 1 year experience in teaching and/or training fiber splicing techniques and cable assemblies
  • Experienced with designing, building, and testing fiber cable assemblies, particularly in cryogen and vacuum conditions
  • Experience performing fiber optic work in environments with limited space or requiring odd positions.
  • Skills:
  • Fiber coating removal
  • Fiber re-coating
  • Specialty fiber splicing
  • Fiber proof-testing
  • Measurement and analysis techniques with optical tools and equipment such as interrogators, optical multiplexers, optical switches, fault locators, OTDR, etc.
  • Knowledgeable about various optics sensing techniques and optical attenuation/insertion loss mechanisms
  • Basic Materials Science knowledge
  • Good communication skills
  • Good attention to detail

• Ability to occasionally lift up to 50 lbs
  • Perform activities:
  • Stooping, typing, standing, or sitting for extended periods of time
  • May need to operate in small confined places in odd locations
  • Work locations could include being on platforms around 25 feet high
  • Dedication to safety to mitigate industrial hazards that may include heat, cold, noise, fumes, strong magnets, lead (Pb), high voltage, and cryogenics
  • Willingness to travel or work required nights/weekends/on-call occasionally

The Field Assembly Manager will ensure that work is executed safely, efficiently, and in accordance with engineering requirements, quality standards, production schedules, and established work instructions. This role requires a strong manufacturing leader who can effectively coordinate multiple skilled trades while working closely with Engineering, Quality, Safety, Supply Chain, and day-shift leadership.

lists.content:
Production Leadership

  • Lead assembly operations supporting tokamak construction and integration
  • Provide direct supervision and coordination of Millwright, Welding, and Electrical union activities
  • Establish priorities for the shift based on the overall production schedule and critical-path activities
  • Ensure work is properly staffed, sequenced, and executed to meet daily and weekly production objectives
  • Monitor production progress throughout the shift and proactively address delays, constraints, and resource issues
  • Conduct shift-start meetings and communicate priorities, safety concerns, schedule requirements, and changes in work scope
  • Maintain strong communication and handoff between day and night shifts
  • Provide detailed shift reports documenting progress, issues, downtime, quality concerns, and outstanding work

    • Skilled Trades Coordination

  • Coordinate work across Millwright, Welding, and Electrical trades to ensure activities are properly sequenced and do not interfere with one another
  • Resolve conflicts between trades and establish clear priorities when multiple activities compete for resources or workspace
  • Work closely with union leadership and shop stewards to ensure effective execution of work while maintaining positive labor relationships
  • Verify that employees are assigned work appropriate to their trade, qualifications, and training
  • Ensure work areas are properly prepared before releasing work to the appropriate trade
  • Coordinate equipment, tooling, materials, permits, and technical information required to complete assigned work

    • Advanced Tokamak Assembly

  • Supervise high-precision mechanical, electrical, structural, and welded assembly activities associated with the tokamak
  • Ensure assembly work is performed according to engineering drawings, specifications, procedures, and approved work instructions
  • Coordinate installation and integration of complex components, systems, and subsystems
  • Work closely with Engineering when drawings, specifications, procedures, or field conditions require clarification.
  • Identify installation issues and escalate technical problems appropriately
  • Support the development and continuous improvement of assembly processes and standard work
  • Maintain a strong focus on configuration control and ensure unauthorized modifications are not made to engineered systems

• Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations, or a related field preferred; equivalent manufacturing leadership experience will be considered
  • 5+ years of experience in a complex manufacturing, assembly, construction, or industrial environment
  • Strong understanding of mechanical, welding, electrical, and industrial assembly processes
  • Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings, specifications, and work instructions
  • Strong understanding of industrial safety practices, including Lockout/Tagout

• Previous supervisory or leadership experience managing skilled trades strongly preferred.
  • Experience working with unionized workforces
  • Experience working in a high-precision or highly engineered manufacturing environment 
  • Experience with Lean manufacturing and continuous-improvement methodologies 
  • Strong computer skills and experience with ERP, MES, scheduling, or production-management systems

• Ability to occasionally lift up to 50 lbs
  • Perform activities such as stooping, climbing, typing, standing, or sitting for extended periods of time
  • Work in a facility that contains industrial hazards including heat, cold, noise, fumes, strong magnets, lead (Pb), high voltage, high current, pressure systems, and cryogenics
  • Willingness to travel or work required nights/weekends/on-call occasionally

Join the power movement as a Field Mechanical Engineer - Assembly
 
As the Field Mechanical Engineer on the Assembly Team at CFS, you will be the co-owner of the SPARC assembly process.  You help guide technicians through any issues that arise along the way and come up with solutions that continue work and assembly moving forward. You will proactively ensure that they have all the tools required for the work, either procuring them off-the-shelf or quickly designing and building small tools and fixtures for use. This also includes the close collaboration with adjacent teams on the Assembly Team, such as creating and incorporating the new process changes with the Assembly Process team or providing the Metrology team with any assistance or tools needed for the precision alignment of coils and other key structures. This role is on-site at Devens, MA but is a “field” role in the sense that you will be working day-to-day in the central construction hall in the CFS-2 facility where we are building the SPARC Tokamak. At the core, your role is to keep the assembly process moving smoothly in all ways using your engineering skills and knowledge to solve the many complex challenges that arise during the assembly process. You will guide how the giant parts of this multi-million pound “swiss-watch” come together!

lists.content:
• Co-own and be the expert in the assembly sequence of your workstation (initially this role is scoped to the assembly of the Toroidal Field Coil (TF) semicircle sub-assemblies), with the responsibility to determine and enact acceptable solutions and changes to the sequence that both allow successful completion of the work-station but also fit with the entire SPARC assembly sequence
  • Be responsible for new first-encounter work scope definition including the installation of various manifolds and magnet sub-assemblies
  • Determine and execute solutions for identified assembly issues that arise, such as fit, method, or component handling problems. Work with the Tokamak System design teams to determine how a part or process step could be modified to work while also meeting functional requirements
  • Proactively procure or build all tools, fixtures, or manipulation equipment required for the upcoming ports of the process in your workstation
  • Serve as the owner for a process by testing, implementing, and handing off to production technicians for repeated use for any given operation or tool(s)
  • Provide design feedback to SPARC sub-system designs with a focus on manufacturing and assembly. Participate in both formal and informal design reviews to ensure what is delivered can be assembled
  • Assist in the disposition and resolution of non-conformance issues on parts or the process, then working to incorporate and release red-line changes into an updated assembly sequence.
  • Support hands on operations during Tokamak Assembly serving a variety of roles in the process
  • Work with teammates in a collaborative fashion to receive feedback early and often to ensure all requirements are met. Many SPARC projects involve high loads, vacuum requirements, and complex manipulation requiring the involvement and review of adjacent sub system experts

• Civil, Mechanical, or Aerospace Engineering B.S. with 5 years' experience
  • 3+ years' of Mechanical Engineering Experience demonstrating project ownership
  • 2+ years' experience overseeing an in-progress construction, manufacturing, or assembly/integration process
  • 2+ years' of experience with CAD software

• 6+ years of Mechanical Engineering Experience demonstrating project ownership
  • Experience with Siemens NX
  • Lifting operations experience
  • Knowledge of welding
  • Knowledge of piping and tubing construction and joining
  • Experience with highly complex or delicate assemblies
  • Experience with assembly or integration in tightly packaged spaces
  • Experience with fast-paced and dynamic construction, manufacturing, or assembly/integration builds
  • Experience with composite preparation, layup, and curing.
  • Experience with cable, tubing, bracing alignment and securing
  • Experience with fiber inspection and splicing work and equipment
  • Heavy component manipulation of large structures

• Ability to occasionally lift up to 50 lbs
  • Perform activities such as typing, standing, stooping, climbing or sitting for extended periods of time
  • Required onsite 5 days/week when assembly operations with relevant tools are underway, with possible alternating first or second shift assignment
  • Work in a facility that contains industrial hazards including heat, cold, noise, fumes, strong magnets, lead (Pb), high voltage, high current, pressure systems, and cryogenics

descriptionBody:
Join the power movement as a Field Mechanical Engineer - Assembly
 

As the Field Mechanical Engineer on the Assembly Team at CFS, you will be the co-owner of the SPARC assembly process.  You help guide technicians through any issues that arise along the way and come up with solutions that continue work and assembly moving forward. You will proactively ensure that they have all the tools required for the work, either procuring them off-the-shelf or quickly designing and building small tools and fixtures for use. This also includes the close collaboration with adjacent teams on the Assembly Team, such as creating and incorporating the new process changes with the Assembly Process team or providing the Metrology team with any assistance or tools needed for the precision alignment of coils and other key structures. This role is on-site at Devens, MA but is a “field” role in the sense that you will be working day-to-day in the central construction hall in the CFS-2 facility where we are building the SPARC Tokamak. At the core, your role is to keep the assembly process moving smoothly in all ways using your engineering skills and knowledge to solve the many complex challenges that arise during the assembly process. You will guide how the giant parts of this multi-million pound “swiss-watch” come together!

lists.content:
• Lead the origination, structuring, negotiation, and execution of long-term power purchase agreements (PPAs), tolling arrangements, environmental product contracts, and capacity contracts for ARC fusion power plants
  • Develop and maintain strategic relationships with key anchor customers, including regulated and municipal utilities, electric cooperatives, hyperscalers, industrial off-takers, and government agencies
  • Formulate and implement the overall wholesale and retail origination strategy to secure contracted revenue streams that support project financing and long-term business objectives
  • Provide commercial leadership during utility procurement processes, competitive solicitations, bilateral negotiations, and RFP responses
  • Collaborate cross-functionally with internal stakeholders—including project development, finance, legal, external affairs, and engineering—to ensure alignment between customer needs, project economics, and deployment strategy
  • Build, mentor, and manage a high-performing team of origination professionals, fostering a culture of excellence, creativity, extreme ownership, and continuous improvement
  • Design and implement innovative contract structures that allow us to effectively engage with early adopters while mitigating the contractual risks in deployment of these novel fusion power plants
  • Identify high-value power markets, RTOs, and favorable regulatory frameworks in which we can execute attractive deals and partnerships
  • Monitor energy market trends, resource plans, and regulatory developments across North American RTOs/ISOs to identify new contracting opportunities and inform market entry plans
  • Develop and own the commercial framework for project opportunities, analyzing market data, assessing risks, and presenting strategic recommendations to executive leadership
  • Represent CFS at industry events, customer meetings, and strategic forums as a subject matter expert and ambassador for fusion energy
  • Oversee post-execution lifecycle management, ensuring rigorous compliance with contractual obligations while nurturing long-term strategic partnerships to maintain operational excellence and corporate good standing
  • Ability to facilitate or source creative solutions and approaches to equitably share risk between parties
  • Prioritize multiple projects and/or issues with conflicting deadlines and/or business unit drivers
  • Demonstrate a reliable and persistent work ethic, seeing tasks through to completion. Stays determined in the face of uncertainty and failure
  • Adaptability to a start-up environment, capability to take initiative, develop own tasks and timelines, and solve broad, ambiguous problems
  • Comfort and capability making judgment calls that are fundamental to the success of entire projects or major initiatives
  • Proven writing and communication ability, and consistent quality of work appropriate for preparing material for a
    broad external audience
  • Can respectfully challenge senior leadership with a well-reasoned and data-supported argument

• Bachelor’s Degree preferably in Engineering, Engineering Technologies, Business, Finance, Economics, Math, Physics or a related field OR > 10+ years of progressive energy industry experience, with at least 5 years specifically leading power origination, structured energy sales, or power marketing
  • Proven track record of originating and closing large-scale, long-term power purchase agreements (PPAs), tolling agreements, environmental product contracts, or capacity contracts
  • Deep technical understanding of North American wholesale power markets, RTO/ISO market rules, transmission dynamics, and commercial risk allocation
  • Established network of executive contacts across utilities, corporate/hyperscaler procurement teams, and wholesale counterparties
  • Strong financial acumen with direct experience working alongside project finance teams to ensure contract bankability and acceptable risk-adjusted returns
  • Superior negotiation, presentation, and communication skills, with a track record of presenting to C-suite executives and investment committees
  • Entrepreneurial mindset with the ability to thrive in a high-growth environment and turn broad, ambiguous opportunities into executed deals

• Master’s degree, MBA, or advanced technical degree preferred
  • Understanding of Global wholesale power markets
  • Experience with clean baseload power, first-of-a-kind (FOAK) technologies, energy storage, or infrastructure
  • Demonstrated experience managing basis risk (nodal vs. zonal pricing splits), shape risk, and congestion/line-loss settlement mechanisms
  • Knowledge of advanced decarbonization procurement standards, such as hourly 24/7 Carbon-Free Energy (CFE) matching and tax credit transferability (e.g., IRA PTC and ITC mechanics).
  • Familiarity with complex utility retail tariffs, standby charges, and wheeling arrangements.
  • Familiarity with federal energy procurement pathways, tax equity structures, or M&A-driven origination
  • Ability to travel up to 40% for customer meetings, site visits, and industry conferences

• Perform activities such as typing, standing, and sitting, for extended periods of time
  • Willingness to occasionally travel or work required nights/weekends/on-call - this position will require up to 25% travel (day-trip & overnight)
  • Work in a facility that contains industrial hazards including heat, cold, noise, fumes, strong magnets, lead (Pb), high voltage, high current, pressure systems, and cryogenics

descriptionPlain:
Join us at the Commonwealth Fusion Systems Somerville hiring events on November 17th or 18th from 5:30 p.m. - 8:00 p.m.
Are you ready to take the next step in your career — and to literally build the future? Apply to join our hiring events at CFS’ facility in Somerville, Massachusetts, on the evenings of Tuesday and Wednesday, Nov. 17 and 18. 
CFS is hiring production technicians in Somerville, MA who can help our work in fusion energy innovation. That means your knack for building cutting-edge hardware and tackling challenging projects can bring a new energy technology to the world and a rewarding paycheck to you.
We’re hiring production technicians at a variety of levels who can work on first, second, and third shifts on weekdays. Second shift comes with a 10% pay differential, and third shifts comes with a 15% pay differential. The pay ranges from $30–$47 per hour before that differential, depending on your experience, and we offer benefits and equity in the company.
We’re moving fast to bring fusion energy to the world and to bring new talent to our company. We’ll be making job offers soon after the fair.
If you’re interested, click APPLY here
Please note: Because space is limited, only those who pass our application stage will receive an invitation to the hiring nights. Our recruiting team will carefully review every registration and if selected, you will receive a confirmation email with your arrival time and full event details. Please only show up if you receive a confirmation email from our team.  


We’re looking for technicians who:
Have 3+ years of experience
Know electromechanical parts and assemblies
Can troubleshoot and resolve manufacturing discrepancies
Can read and interpret assembly drawings, wiring diagrams, with great attention to detail
The specific pay differentials are:
Weekday first shift (Monday-Friday, 6:00 p.m. - 3:00 p.m.): no differential
Weekday second shift (Monday-Friday, 2:30 p.m. - 11:30 p.m.): 10%
Weekday third shift (Monday–Friday, 10 p.m. – 7:00 a.m.): 15%
What to bring:
Updated resume that highlights your skills and experiences
Closed-toe shoes
Any questions you have about working at CFS, our roles, or the hiring process
At the hiring event, you’ll also be able to meet our employees to learn more about our fusion energy future.

The Environmental Health & Safety Engineering Intern contributes to building the environmental, health, and safety culture for the fusion industry. This role offers hands-on experience in a dynamic R&D, plant, and manufacturing environment. Our intern will support critical projects across Environmental Protection, Health, and Safety, helping to ensure a safe, compliant, and sustainable workplace. Responsibilities will include assisting with environmental reporting and compliance initiatives, program audits and process confirmations, and equivalent.

lists.content:
• 13-26 week internship
  • 40-50 hours per week with set hourly salary based on year in school
  • Opportunities on site in Devens, MA. If an intern is going to be on site, you will be responsible for your own transportation and housing
  • Specific project assignments and required technical skillset will vary based on the team’s existing need.
  • Opportunities available for currently enrolled college students in all levels of schooling from bachelor’s degree to PhD
  • Interns must be authorized to work in the United States for any employer

• Help collect, organize, and prepare data for recurring regulatory filings
  • Keep digital filing systems, permit records, hazardous waste manifests, and Safety Data Sheet (SDS) libraries up to date and audit-ready
  • Conduct audits of existing programs or processes across Environmental, Health, and Safety
  • Conduct site inspections to support EHS programs and confirm compliance or identify improvements needed
  • Participate in team meetings, help draft topic-based awareness bulletins or toolbox talks, and support EHS training across the organization

• Pursuing a Bachelor’s or Master’s Degree in EHS, Environmental Engineering, Industrial Hygiene, Chemistry, or a related STEM field
  • Foundational knowledge of core EHS regulatory frameworks (OSHA, EPA) through coursework or academic projects
  • Ability to work in a high-volume, fast paced environment
  • Prior internship or hands-on experience in an industrial, chemical, laboratory, or construction setting
  • Familiarity with specific environmental regulatory standards (RCRA, SWPPP, Tier II/TRI, DEC)
  • Demonstrated proficiency in Excel or data management tools for compiling records and reporting metrics
  • Strong organizational skills with the ability to handle shifting priorities under general supervision
  • Baseline familiarity with environmental, health, and safety regulations (e.g., OSHA, EPA, RCRA, DEC) gained through coursework or prior projects is required

• Willingness to travel or work required nights/weekends/on-call occasionally
  • Perform activities such as typing, standing, or sitting for extended periods of time
  • Dedication to safety to mitigate industrial hazards that may include heat, cold, noise, fumes, strong magnets, lead (Pb), high voltage, and cryogenics

salaryDescription:

For BS interns, the hourly rate is $25–$32
For MS/PhD interns, the rate is $35–$38
 
Benefits included for full-time interns:
•     40 hours of sick time
•     Health, dental, and vision insurance
•     401(k) with employer matching (must be 21 years of age to enroll)
•     Professional growth opportunities
•     Team-building activities

lists.content:
• 17-26 week internship
  • 40-50 hours per week with set hourly salary based on year in school
  • Opportunities on site in Devens, MA. If an intern is going to be on site, you will be responsible for your own transportation and housing
  • Specific project assignments and required technical skillset will vary based on the team’s existing need.
  • Opportunities available for currently enrolled college students in all levels of schooling from bachelor’s degree to PhD
  • Interns must be authorized to work in the United States for any employer

We currently have multiple openings for the Electrical/Electromechanical Engineering Internship on the Electrical Engineering Team. Please note that the following list encompasses all available roles, so individual responsibilities will vary depending on the specific position:
  • Test and debug electronics and RF hardware on the bench
  • Analyze test data in Python
  • Install and commission plant hardware
  • Create test plans for the validation and commissioning of electrical equipment
  • Test result collection & analysis
  • Electrical drawing review and redline
  • Technical analysis of electrical design projects and specification creation
  • Mechanical electrical cabinets build, installation, and electrical technician support vendor and field work
  • Electromechanical System Documentation, generate assembly instructions, test procedures
  • Aid the setup and running of bench top tests
  • CAD 3D modeling

Please note that the list below encompasses the requirements for all available roles, so individual requirements will vary depending on the specific position:
  • Pursuing a degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Electromechanical Engineering, or Power Electronics
  • Hands-on experience with hand tools, power tools, or test equipment
  • Basic electrical knowledge and experience with 2D and 3D CAD software (e.g., NX, SolidWorks)
  • Participation in hands-on student design teams
  • Experience with lab instruments such as oscilloscopes, spectrum/network analyzers, signal generators, and bench power supplies
  • RF, microwave, or antenna coursework, or amateur radio experience
  • Proficiency in Python for test automation and data analysis
  • Experience with schematic capture, PCB layout, or SPICE simulation
  • Skills in soldering, cable assembly, or panel wiring (e.g., from Formula SAE, rocketry, solar car, or similar design teams)
  • Prior co-op or internship experience in power electronics, test engineering, or hardware development

• Perform activities such as typing, standing, or sitting for extended periods of time
  • Dedication to safety to mitigate industrial hazards that may include heat, cold, noise, fumes, strong magnets, lead (Pb), high voltage, and cryogenics
