We are looking for a talented I&C and Network Engineering Intern to join our team! CFS interns are highly valued within the organization and placed into meaningful and challenging roles.

lists.content:
• 13-26 week internship
  • 40-50 hours per week with set hourly salary based on year in school
  • Opportunities on site in Devens, MA. If an intern is going to be on site, you will be responsible for your own transportation and housing
  • Specific project assignments and required technical skillset will vary based on the team’s existing need.
  • Opportunities available for currently enrolled college students in all levels of schooling from bachelor’s degree to PhD
  • Interns must be authorized to work in the United States for any employer

• Develop and maintain network architecture and rack elevation drawings using CAD
  • Support installation and configuration of network equipment
  • Perform field walkdowns and support network installation, troubleshooting, and commissioning activities
  • Test and commission network infrastructure

• Pursuing an engineering degree with focus in the fields of Information Technology (IT) / Computer Information Systems, Network Engineering / Cybersecurity, Computer Science
  • A strong technical foundation
  • CAD experience
  • Interest in networking and controls infrastructure, and a willingness to work hands-on in the field
  • Eager to learn and comfortable working across both engineering design and field execution.

• Willingness to travel or work required nights/weekends/on-call occasionally
  • Perform activities such as typing, standing, or sitting for extended periods of time
  • Dedication to safety to mitigate industrial hazards that may include heat, cold, noise, fumes, strong magnets, lead (Pb), high voltage, and cryogenics

salaryDescription:

•     40 hours of sick time

•     Professional growth opportunities
•     Team-building activities

Join the power movement as a Materials Test Engineering Intern
 
The CFS Materials Team is seeking a motivated Materials Test Engineering Intern to join our cutting-edge team. In this role, you will support the development and testing of advanced materials critical to key tokamak systems such as plasma-facing components, the vacuum vessel, and high field magnets. This is a unique opportunity to work at the forefront of sustainable energy innovation in a collaborative, fast-paced R&D environment.

lists.content:
• 13-18 week internship
  • 40-50 hours per week with set hourly salary based on year in school
  • Opportunities on site in Devens, MA. If an intern is going to be on site, you will be responsible for your own transportation and housing
  • Specific project assignments and required technical skillset will vary based on the team’s existing need.
  • Opportunities available for currently enrolled college students in all levels of schooling from bachelor’s degree to PhD
  • Interns must be authorized to work in the United States for any employer

• Support day-to-day operations and test development work in the Materials Test Lab, including sample preparation, test execution, data collection, and analysis
  • Work alongside engineers and technicians to enable material performance evaluation for critical fusion components
  • Contribute to custom test development projects
  • Example projects may include: commissioning a new vacuum furnace, designing and testing a new polishing and etching recipe for novel materials, troubleshooting complex test equipment to enable renewed testing campaigns, creating and implementing methods to extract grain size or inclusion or other data from SEM or optical images, and working with FTIR
    •

• Pursuing an engineering degree with focus in the field of Materials Engineering or Mechanical Engineering
  • Experience with FTIR, Optical and SEM imaging and polishing and sample preparation
  • Interest or experience with materials science, metallurgy, mechanical engineering, mechanical testing, electrical engineering, physics, chemistry, nanoscience, microscopy, engineering lab work, or instrumentation
  • Hands-on or engineering project experience or hands-on experience with materials testing and characterization equipment and testing procedures is preferred
  • Demonstration of exceptional results through a range of different pursuits
  • High self-motivation and drive to execute quickly with excellent troubleshooting/problem-solving skills

• Willingness to travel or work required nights/weekends/on-call occasionally
  • Perform activities such as typing, standing, or sitting for extended periods of time
  • Dedication to safety to mitigate industrial hazards that may include heat, cold, noise, fumes, strong magnets, lead (Pb), high voltage, and cryogenics

  • 40-50 hours per week with set hourly salary based on year in school

We currently have multiple openings for the Mechanical or Magnet Engineering Internship. Please note that the following list encompasses all available roles, so individual responsibilities will vary depending on the specific position:
  • Tooling and Hardware Design - Accelerate magnet production and SPARC assembly via design, first principles analysis, and rapid prototyping
  • Multiphysics and Structural Analysis - Develop optimization tools and perform design optimization and cost reduction for next generation magnet systems and tokamak structures
  • Prototyping and Next-Gen Architecture Optimization - Fabricate and iterate on next-generation designs to inform design-for-manufacturing (DFM) and design-for-assembly (DFA) trade studies, cost reduction, and commercialization of fusion systems

• Pursuing a degree with focus in the field of Mechanical Engineering
  • Prior experience with 3D CAD, machine shop, rapid prototyping and assembly, first-principles structural and thermal analysis, active participation and hands on experience on student teams (Formula SAE, Rocket Club, etc)
  • Demonstration of exceptional results through a range of different pursuits
  • High self-motivation and drive to execute quickly with excellent troubleshooting/problem-solving skills
  • Communication - not afraid to ask for help, shows evidence that they’d integrate nicely into a team of technical engineers / scientists, but also able to communicate with people with less of a technical background, like technicians, supply chain, etc

If that’s you and this role fits, we want to hear from you.


Join the power movement as Lead Assembly Technician 
 
As a Lead Technician on the Assembly Team at CFS, you will be responsible for overseeing and organizing the small technician teams to conduct all assembly activities to construct the SPARC Tokamak. This includes the handling, alignment, and mechanical integration of large electromagnetic coils, vacuum vessels, instrumentation systems, support structures, tooling and manipulation equipment, diagnostic systems, and superconducting cable bundles, all together into a tightly packed and highly integrated central device. You will use your extensive experience in building and handling large equipment, structures, or plant systems to facilitate the efficient and high-quality completion of SPARC. You will organize the day-to-day work orders of the day per the schedule, assign technicians to each set of work, adjust as needed from previous work or issues, give morning briefs and shift hand-off reports, and overall guide all activity in the assembly work areas. During this you will work directly and collaboratively with the engineers, the metrology group, the quality group, and many other team-members to ensure correct and precise completion of the components and identify and help resolve issues as they arise during the build process. You will work with other technicians and leads, working in a dynamic and flexible workplace that shifts focus and priority as needed to meet the schedule to complete our next-generation tokamak device.
 
This role is truly a once in a lifetime opportunity to use your hands-on assembly skills to accelerate the development of fusion energy by ensuring SPARC is built on time and to high quality!
 
Hours: 6:00 am - 2:30 pm, over time may be available

lists.content:
• Day-to-day activity management and coordination of the technician teams to complete the assembly operations, per the overall schedule
  • Work order review, including mechanical, welding, electrical, and lifting tasks
  • Participation in major on-site operations, such as important component lifts and movements
  • Inspection buy-off (visual confirmation only) for tasks completed by the technician teams
  • Daily updates to the rest of the Assembly team on status of each operation or work orders and what was completed that day
  • Assignment of each technician or technician team to specific operations and work orders, as needed for the schedule priorities determined by the planning
  • Coordination with out-of-house work teams working on specialized sections of SPARC assembly when they arrive, ensuring that all teams can efficiently complete their work on time
  • General troubleshooting of any issues with assembly as they arrive, and coming up with workarounds to problems, or elevating the issue as necessary. Assistance in all aspects that helps and keeps the technician teams moving forward as smoothly as possible
  • Notification to Assembly Engineers of problems or need for non-conformance reports in a specific assembly Coordination with the Assembly Testing Team on their upcoming or ongoing activities, to ensure that each day all teams can efficiently and safely complete their work
  • Daily kick-off meetings and shift-change meetings to outline what is being done that shift, which team is working on what, what the major important events (like big lifts) are that need to be communicated, safety hazards of the day, and all other details that will help the teams work efficiently and safely

• High school diploma or equivalent experience
  • 7+ years in a highly technical assembly role; e.g., aerospace/aircraft, semiconductor, oil & gas, power plants, wind, racing & automotive
  • 2 to 3 years overseeing a team of five people or more
  • Experience completing large scale projects end to end
  • Experience assisting lifting operations
  • Knowledge of standard joining and integration methods (bolted interfaces and flanges, welding, epoxies, etc.)
  • Highly self-motivated, organized, and passionate about their work
  • Highly safety conscious

• 10+ years in a highly technical assembly role; e.g., aerospace/aircraft, semiconductor, oil & gas, power plants, wind, racing & automotive
  • 3+ years leading a team of ten people or more
  • Can operate a forklift
  • Ability to use basic machining tools; e.g., lathe/mill
  • Experience creating designs for tooling
  • Experience using JIRA, Manufacturo, or other software based tracking
  • Experience with organizing rigging and direct oversight of heavy components lifting
  • Knowledge of rigging and lifting best practice
  • Knowledge of vacuum systems and clean room best practices
  • Knowledge of cryogenic systems
  • Prior experience in independent design and construction of small fixtures and tooling
  • Experience with metrology tools and precision alignment of components
  • Willingness to occasionally travel for required nights/weekends/on-call
  • Dedication to safety

• Ability to occasionally lift up to 50 lbs
  • Perform activities:
  • Stooping, typing, standing, or sitting for extended periods of time
  • May need to operate in small confined places in odd locations
  • Work locations could include being on platforms around 25 feet high
  • Dedication to safety to mitigate industrial hazards that may include heat, cold, noise, fumes, strong magnets, lead (Pb), high voltage, and cryogenics
  • Willingness to travel or work required nights/weekends/on-call occasionally

descriptionBody:
Join the power movement as Lead Assembly Technician 
 
As a Lead Technician on the Assembly Team at CFS, you will be responsible for overseeing and organizing the small technician teams to conduct all assembly activities to construct the SPARC Tokamak. This includes the handling, alignment, and mechanical integration of large electromagnetic coils, vacuum vessels, instrumentation systems, support structures, tooling and manipulation equipment, diagnostic systems, and superconducting cable bundles, all together into a tightly packed and highly integrated central device. You will use your extensive experience in building and handling large equipment, structures, or plant systems to facilitate the efficient and high-quality completion of SPARC. You will organize the day-to-day work orders of the day per the schedule, assign technicians to each set of work, adjust as needed from previous work or issues, give morning briefs and shift hand-off reports, and overall guide all activity in the assembly work areas. During this you will work directly and collaboratively with the engineers, the metrology group, the quality group, and many other team-members to ensure correct and precise completion of the components and identify and help resolve issues as they arise during the build process. You will work with other technicians and leads, working in a dynamic and flexible workplace that shifts focus and priority as needed to meet the schedule to complete our next-generation tokamak device.
 
This role is truly a once in a lifetime opportunity to use your hands-on assembly skills to accelerate the development of fusion energy by ensuring SPARC is built on time and to high quality!
 
Weekday third shift (Monday–Friday, 10 p.m. – 6:30 a.m.)
Hourly pay + 15% Differential

Join the power movement as Lead Piping Engineer

As the Lead Piping Engineer, you will lead all piping engineering functions, including pipe stress analysis, piping standards and material specifications, and pipe support design. Depending on project needs and team structure, perform these engineering activities directly or provide technical leadership by overseeing, coordinating, and delegating work to the piping engineering team or contractors.

lists.content:
Pipe Stress Engineering
  • Establish and document pipe stress methodologies, standards, and best practices
  • Perform pipe stress analyses using industry-standard pipe stress software (e.g., AutoPIPE)
  • Evaluate piping systems for sustained, thermal expansion, occasional, seismic, wind, and dynamic loading conditions
  • Design and specify pipe support systems, including spring supports, restraints, guides, anchors, and hangers
  • Develop, maintain, and continuously improve the company's standard pipe support catalog
  • Prepare and maintain piping stress calculations, reports, design documentation, and supporting engineering records
  • Ensure piping designs comply with applicable codes and standards, including ASME B31.1, ASME B31.3, and other relevant industry standards
  • Coordinate with piping designers, mechanical engineers, civil/structural engineers, equipment engineers, and project teams to optimize piping layouts and support configurations
  • Evaluate equipment nozzle loads and ensure compliance with vendor allowable loads and applicable standards
  • Perform fatigue assessment and analysis for piping systems and components subjected to cyclic operating conditions
  • Conduct creep evaluations of piping systems operating within the creep temperature range to ensure long-term integrity over the plant's design life
  • Perform dynamic and pulsation analyses of suction and discharge piping systems to verify operational reliability and compliance with design requirements
  • Evaluate piping systems for vibration susceptibility and develop engineering solutions to mitigate vibration-related issues
  • Collaborate with equipment vendors to integrate pulsation dampeners and ensure compatibility with piping system design and performance requirements
  • Recommend design modifications to minimize piping stresses and improve system reliability and constructability
  • Perform buckling calculations on vacuum piping systems
  • Review vendor drawings, equipment data, and support details for compliance with project requirements
    • Pipe Specification and Material Engineering
    • Develop, maintain, and standardize company-wide piping material specifications
    • Establish material selection philosophies and engineering best practices
    • Select piping materials based on process conditions, operating temperatures and pressures, corrosion, erosion, fluid compatibility, and applicable codes
    • Prepare piping material specifications, valve specifications, specialty item specifications, and procurement documentation
    • Ensure piping materials comply with applicable codes, standards, and project requirements, including ASME, ASTM, API, MSS, NACE, and other applicable industry standards
    • Perform material compatibility and corrosion evaluations for process and utility piping systems
    • Review, evaluate, and approve piping specification deviations and technical exceptions
    • Support value engineering initiatives by evaluating alternative materials and products while maintaining compliance and reliability
    • Support procurement activities

      • Supervisory Responsibilities:

    • Serve as technical authority for piping engineering within the organization
    • Plan, prioritize, and coordinate pipe engineering resources to support project schedules, including staffing, resource forecasting, and workload planning
    • Assign, oversee, and review work performed by internal engineers, contractors, and third-party engineering firms
    • Ensure piping engineering deliverables are completed on schedule and meet company quality standards
    • Participate in interdisciplinary design reviews, HAZOPs, constructability and design reviews
    • Provide technical guidance and mentoring to piping engineers and designers
    • Interface with clients, equipment vendors, contractors, and regulatory agencies on piping engineering matters

• Bachelor’s degree in mechanical engineering, structural engineering, or equivalent engineering program from an accredited four (4) year university or equivalent work experience
  • Minimum ten (10) years of job-related experience in piping engineering, including pipe stress analysis and piping materials/specifications
  • Strong knowledge of applicable codes and standards, including ASME B31.1, ASME B31.3, MSS, ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code, ASTM, API, MSS, NACE, WRC-537, and ISO
  • Experience using pipe stress analysis software, preferably AutoPIPE. Experience with CAESAR II, ROHR, or PEPS is also acceptable
  • Experience selecting materials for high-temperature service, molten salt systems, cryogenic applications, vacuum piping systems, corrosive environments, and pressure-containing systems
  • Ability to communicate effectively with a variety of audiences, including management, coworkers, vendors, and contractors
  • Proficiency with standard computer applications, including Google Workspace, Microsoft Word, Microsoft Excel, web browsers, and email applications
  • Experience with Navisworks is preferred

• Professional Engineer (PE) license or ability to obtain licensure
  • Experience with Navisworks
  • Experience with 3D plant design software (e.g., Plant 3D, SmartPlant, AVEVA E3D, or CADWorx)
  • Experience in power generation, industrial process facilities, chemical processing, molten salt systems, or energy projects

• Perform activities such as stooping, climbing, typing, standing, or sitting for extended periods of time
  • Dedication to safety to mitigate industrial hazards that may include heat, cold, noise, fumes, strong magnets, lead (Pb), high voltage, and cryogenics
  • Willingness to travel or work required nights/weekends/on-call occasionally

lists.content:
• Execute complex testing procedures in the field with a primary focus on mechanical testing to include pneumatic pressure proofing and leak detection using helium leak detector.
  • Work under the direction of Manager, Assembly Testing, to execute test procedures
  • Serve as front line supervisor for test technicians by providing guidance and instruction to technicians to facilitate safe, effective, and efficient execution of work
  • Identify issues and potential issues pro-actively, ensure accurate submission to our work and quality management systems and assist to drive issues to successful conclusions
  • Ensure completion of all test documentation in an accurate and timely fashion
  • Coach technicians to embody the CFS behaviors and guiding principles in all interactions
  • Represent the SASY Test team in collaboration with all CFS cross-functional teams as required
  • Adhere to the highest standards of safety and ensure that activities taking place are being performed in accordance with CFS safety policies and applicable regulatory safety standards

• HS Diploma
  • Minimum 5 years of hands-on mechanical testing experience, with a heavy focus on pneumatic pressure proofing and helium leak detection using mass spectrometers.
  • Proven experience leading small to medium-sized crews of technicians performing complex mechanical or testing activities.
  • Demonstrated experience with high-vacuum hardware: Must be proficient in plumbing temporary test fixtures and making connections using KF, CF, VCR, compression fittings, and NPT.
  • Familiarity with setting up and connecting vacuum systems, including turbomolecular pumps and leak detectors.
  • Mid-level proficiency in with Microsoft or Google productivity software

• Formal training (40+ hours) or active progression toward an ASNT Level II NDT certification in Leak Testing.
  • Direct experience with specific leak testing methodologies (e.g., tracer probe, hood technique, and helium-filled object techniques).
  • Prior experience working in fusion-relevant, aerospace, or semiconductor cleanroom environments.
  • Experience with low or high voltage electrical testing

• Ability to occasionally lift up to 50 lbs
  • Perform activities such as stooping, climbing, typing, standing, or sitting for extended periods of time
  • Work in a facility that contains industrial hazards including heat, cold, noise, fumes, strong magnets, lead (Pb), high voltage, high current, pressure systems, and cryogenics

lists.content:
• Safely program, set-up and operate multiple CNC equipment with minimal assistance

  • Read and adhere to all verbal and written processes

  • Perform daily preventative maintenance on equipment

• Formal trades or apprenticeship programs

  • Basic knowledge of welding and torches
  • Knowledge of how to use a plasma cutter
  • Basic knowledge of sheet metal fabrication
  • Trained in time management

• Knowledge of how to calculate tolerance changes to atmospheric temperature changes in shops (CTE)

  • Experience with Haas machining centers
  • 4 and 5 axis machining experience

• Ability to lift up to 50 lbs

  • Perform activities such as typing, standing, or sitting for extended periods of time

Join the power movement as Manager, Process Engineering - Assembly 
 
The Manager, Process Engineering is an organizational leader accountable for the management, engineering oversight, and efficient development and release of all engineering created work instructions across all elements of the SPARC Tokamak build. The role will manage a team of 8 to 15 engineers spread across the in work and soon to start stations of SPARC Assembly. As manager, the role at its core requires supporting the effective organization, tasking, and development of the individual contributors on the team while also driving efficiency and technical development tools to most effectively complete the thousands of planning tasks prior to the planned start of work. Additionally, the leadership role requires close collaboration with Field Assembly Engineering peers (who scope and discretize the work) and design engineering counterparts supplying inputs and technical detail. The role involves a high degree and quantity of decision making around technical approaches to a wide variety of mechanical challenges to keep the team unblocked and on task. At the core, the manager will refine existing processes, develop individual talent, and resolve pop up issues to create the most complete set of work instructions needed to build CFS’s technically complex SPARC Tokmakak.

The Manager, Process Engineering is an organizational leader accountable for the management, engineering oversight, and efficient development and release of all engineering created work instructions across all elements of the SPARC Tokamak build. The role will manage a team of 8 to 15 engineers spread across the in work and soon to start stations of SPARC Assembly. As manager, the role at its core requires supporting the effective organization, tasking, and development of the individual contributors on the team while also driving efficiency and technical development tools to most effectively complete the thousands of planning tasks prior to the planned start of work. lists.content:
• Lead a team of eight to fifteen process engineers to develop, release and implement the technical engineering work instruction to construct the SPARC device
  • Translate department-level strategy into actionable group objectives and manageable project timelines
  • Define and optimize process engineering workflows and internal standards to improve successful solution outcome rate and team efficiency
  • Oversee the full development of tracking and priority tools to concurrently manage hundreds of individual planning tasks for the SPARC Assembly effort.
  • Establish and reinforce best practices for mechanical assembly, including standards for aligning, installation, and rework
  • Manage all aspects of the group's talent, including hiring, training, and setting clear performance expectations
  • Coach and mentor team members, actively contributing to their technical growth and professional career development
  • Build relationships across the organization to influence design direction and resolve technical conflicts with stakeholders
  • Provide design feedback to SPARC sub-system designs with a focus on manufacturing and assembly. Participate in both formal and informal design reviews to ensure what is delivered can be assembled
  • Support hands on operations during Tokamak Assembly serving a variety of roles in the process
  • Work with teammates in a collaborative fashion to receive feedback early and often to ensure all requirements are met. Many SPARC projects involve high loads, vacuum requirements, and complex manipulation requiring the involvement and review of adjacent sub system experts

• Civil, Structural, Mechanical, or Aerospace Engineering BS
  • 7+ years of Mechanical Engineering Experience demonstrating project ownership
  • 2+ years experience directly managing an engineering team or a large scale engineering project as an individual contributor.
  • 2+ years of experience with CAD software

• 8+ years of Mechanical Engineering Experience demonstrating project ownership
  • 4+ years experience directly managing an engineering team or a large scale engineering project as an individual contributor
  • 3 years of experience with Siemens NX
  • Lifting operations experience
  • Knowledge of welding
  • Knowledge of piping and tubing construction and joining
  • Experience with highly complex or delicate assemblies
  • Experience with assembly or integration in tightly packaged spaces
  • Experience with fast-paced and dynamic construction, manufacturing, or assembly/integration builds

• Ability to occasionally lift up to 50 lbs
  • Perform activities such as typing, standing, stooping, climbing or sitting for extended periods of time
  • Travel occasionally required for vendor visits during tool fabrication phases
  • Required onsite 5 days/week when assembly operations with relevant tools are underway, with possible first or second shift assignment
  • Work in a facility that contains industrial hazards including heat, cold, noise, fumes, strong magnets, lead (Pb), high voltage, high current, pressure systems, and cryogenics

Join the power movement as a Manufacturing Engineer

As a Manufacturing Engineer at CFS, you will play a crucial role in transitioning new products from development to full-scale production. You will work closely with cross-functional teams, including product design, quality assurance, supply chain, and production, to ensure the introduction of new products to manufacturing. The ideal candidate has a strong engineering background, excellent problem-solving skills, and experience with moving products from R&D into manufacturing.

lists.content:
• Collaborate with product design and development teams to develop and understand product specifications, requirements, and manufacturing challenges
  • Develop, implement, and qualify manufacturing processes for new products, ensuring they meet quality, cost, and production rate targets
  • Design and optimize production layouts, tooling, and fixtures to support efficient manufacturing
  • Conduct Design for Manufacturing (DFM) and Design for Assembly (DFA) analysis to improve product design
  • Create and maintain process documentation, including work instructions, process flow diagrams, pFMEA’s, and standard operating procedures (SOPs)
  • Coordinate with the supply chain and planning teams to source components and materials, ensuring timely delivery and compliance with quality standards
  • Develop, monitor and analyze manufacturing performance metrics to identify and implement continuous improvement opportunities
  • Provide hands-on training and support to production personnel on work instructions, processes, equipment, and best practices
  • Troubleshoot and resolve production and quality issues, collaborating with relevant teams to ensure timely resolution
  • Ensure compliance with safety regulations and quality standards

• Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Industrial Engineering, or equivalent work experience
  • 5+ years of experience in manufacturing engineering, with experience transitioning products from R&D to manufacturing
  • Experience with Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, or other process improvement methodologies
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work effectively in cross-functional teams
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with a detail-oriented approach
  • Ability to work in a fast-paced, dynamic environment and manage multiple priorities

• Experience with magnets, thermo-mechanical assemblies, machining, welding, and/or vacuum systems
  • Experience with the application of Lean and/or Six Sigma methodologies
  • Experience writing and developing equipment specifications and maintenance plan
  • Experience with CAD software
  • Proficiency in work instruction writing, material planning, process mapping, and capacity modeling
  • Ability to read and understand technical drawings, incl. GD&T and tolerance stack-ups
  • High self-motivation and drive to execute quickly with excellent troubleshooting/ problem-solving skills

• Ability to lift up to 50 lbs occasionally
  • Perform activities such as typing, standing, stooping, and sitting, for extended periods of time
  • Dedication to safety to mitigate hazards that may include heat, cold, noise, fumes, strong magnets, lead, high voltage, and cryogenics
  • Willingness to occasionally travel or work required nights/weekends/on-call

As a third shift Manufacturing Engineer, you will be part of the on-shift manufacturing engineering team for our superconducting magnet production line, where advanced magnet components are fabricated, inspected, assembled, and tested. The Schedule:
Shift: Monday through Friday, 10:00 pm - 6:30 am
 
15% differential add to base pay

lists.content:

  • Troubleshoot process, equipment, and quality issues, and decide when to hold or stop work to protect product and people

  • Root cause analysis and nonconformance management
  • MES and work instruction use

  • Experience with instrumentation such as voltage taps, cryogenic temperature sensors, or fiber optic sensing, and with data acquisition and time-series tools

  • Welding and NDT (VT, RT, UT)

lists.content:
• Act autonomously as the primary owner of cable magnet hardware for SPARC, ARC, or other projects, ensuring designs are completed, validated, procured, built, and installed correctly and on time
  • Produce new and iterate on existing design concepts, using a deep understanding of physics, structural mechanics, and analysis techniques for both metallics and composites
  • Liaise with partner teams such as R&D, analysis, manufacturing, and procurement to drive completion of program milestones in a timely fashion
  • Diagnose issues on the production and assembly line and provide immediate path forward based on known understanding of hardware. Propose and implement design solutions based on root cause
  • Prepare reports, presentations, and other documentation to serve as design documentation and validation of final Cable Magnet systems

• Bachelor’s degree in mechanical engineering, aerospace engineering, or another relevant field
  • A minimum of 5 years of engineering design and analysis experience is required, including at least 2 years providing engineering support to production hardware in the form of resolving technical issues and implementing design for manufacturing or assembly changes
  • Relevant hands-on experience in the form of parts designed for high loads and/or extreme environments 
  • Excellent fundamental knowledge of mechanical systems such as static structures and heat transfer
    Familiarity with all steps in the design process with an emphasis on creativity, simplicity, and execution 
  • Be self-motivated, committed to self-growth, and exhibit excellent problem-solving skills 
  • CAD proficiency (required) NX preferred, any acceptable
  • FEA (required) ANSYS and COMSOL preferred

• Demonstrated record of design of mechanical components beyond desktop scale. E.g. high power (MW+), high mass (ton+), high force (MN+)

lists.content:

  • Experience modeling chemical systems (e.g. reaction, transport, thermodynamic, radiochemical)

 You are accountable for the successful execution of all NDT inspections across CFS manufacturing, CFS-2 construction, tokamak assembly, and vendor sites, spanning UT/UTPA, RT (CR & DR), ET, PT, MT, and VT. lists.content:
• Develop and maintain organizational NDT capabilities, identifying gaps in technology or competency and implementing solutions that scale from SPARC manufacturing and assembly into the future ARC fleet
  • Partner with corporate EHS Radiation Safety to ensure safe and compliant industrial radiography operations
  • Act as the Responsible Level III and Certifying Authority, maintaining overall responsibility for the NDT personnel qualification and certification program
  • Oversee NDT execution across CFS manufacturing, CFS-2 construction, tokamak assembly, and vendor sites, ensuring safety, compliance, and alignment with project schedules
  • Oversee and audit NDT technicians to ensure examinations are conducted in accordance with work instructions and are aligned with engineering requirements & applicable codes and standards
  • Work directly with the NDT engineering and training team to help establish technician training and competency to new procedures and standards
  • Participate in establishing and maintaining training and qualification frameworks for NDT technicians, and provide ongoing technical support and troubleshooting
  • Review and audit work order instructions and procedures to ensure the latest is used for examinations
  • Use NDT results to inform nonconformances and RCCA, and drive the continuous improvement of NDT capabilities to feed lessons learned back into process and design improvements for future projects

• 3+ years in a managerial or supervisory capacity
  • Level III certification (ASNT, NAS 410, or ISO 9712) in UT/PAUT and RT
  • Working knowledge of surface and visual methods (PT, MT, VT) sufficient to oversee, audit, and certify technicians in those methods

Join the power movement as an Operations Coordinator - Assembly

The SASY Assembly Coordinator provides administrative and operational support to the Field Assembly organization, with primary responsibility for purchasing production consumables and supplies, maintaining organization and availability of clean room materials, coordinating new-hire onboarding, and leading clean room training. This position serves as an important link between Assembly, Purchasing, Quality, Human Resources, and other functional teams to ensure employees have the materials, training, and support necessary to operate safely, efficiently, and in compliance with company requirements.

The ideal candidate is highly organized, detail-oriented, proactive, and comfortable working in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.

lists.content:
Production Supplies & Purchasing

  • Manage purchasing of production consumables, supplies, PPE, office supplies, and other operational materials
  • Monitor inventory levels and reorder materials to prevent production interruptions
  • Obtain quotes, place purchase orders, and communicate with suppliers regarding orders, deliveries, and shortages
  • Maintain accurate purchasing and inventory records
  • Identify opportunities to reduce costs, improve purchasing efficiency, and standardize commonly used supplies
  • Work closely with Assembly leadership to anticipate upcoming material requirements

    • Clean Room Supply Management

    • Maintain organization, cleanliness, and inventory of clean room supplies and materials
    • Ensure required PPE, garments, gloves, wipes, cleaning materials, and other clean room consumables are readily available
    • Establish and maintain organized storage locations and visual inventory controls
    • Monitor usage and develop appropriate reorder points and inventory levels
    • Support adherence to clean room procedures and company quality requirements
    • Coordinate replenishment of clean room supplies to minimize disruption to production

      • New-Hire Onboarding

      • Coordinate administrative activities associated with new employee onboarding
      • Work with Human Resources and department leadership to ensure new hires have required documentation, equipment, PPE, and access prior to starting
      • Coordinate first-day activities, facility orientation, and required production training
      • Maintain onboarding checklists and training documentation
      • Communicate new-hire schedules and requirements to appropriate departments
        • Clean Room Training
        • Lead and coordinate clean room training for new and existing employees
        • Train employees on proper gowning, PPE, clean room behavior, material handling, housekeeping, and applicable procedures
        • Ensure employees understand and follow established clean room requirements
        • Maintain accurate training records and communicate training completion to appropriate personnel
        • Coordinate refresher training when required
        • Work with Quality and Operations to identify and address training gaps

          • General Administrative Support

          • Provide day-to-day administrative support to the Assembly team
          • Maintain production-related records, spreadsheets, forms, and documentation
          • Assist with scheduling meetings, communications, and department coordination
          • Support audits and documentation activities as needed
          • Track department action items and follow up on outstanding requests
          • Assist with implementation of process improvements and standard work
          • Perform other administrative and operational duties as assigned

• High school diploma or equivalent required; associate degree preferred
  • 5+ years of experience in a manufacturing, production, operations, or administrative environment preferred
  • Experience working in a clean room or regulated manufacturing environment is a plus
  • Strong organizational and time-management skills
  • Excellent attention to detail
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office, particularly Excel and Outlook
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities and work effectively with employees at all levels
  • Ability to work independently while also functioning effectively as part of a cross-functional team
  • Strong problem-solving and follow-through skills

• Experience with purchasing or procurement
  • Experience with inventory management
  • Experience with ERP or purchasing systems
  • Previous experience training employees
  • Knowledge of clean room procedures and GMP/quality requirements

• Ability to occasionally lift up to 50 lbs
  • Perform activities such as stooping, climbing, typing, standing, or sitting for extended periods of time
  • Work in a facility that contains industrial hazards including heat, cold, noise, fumes, strong magnets, lead (Pb), high voltage, high current, pressure systems, and cryogenics
  • Willingness to travel or work required nights/weekends/on-call occasionally

Join the power movement as Power Business Research and Analytics Manager

Commonwealth Fusion Systems is moving fusion power out of the laboratory and onto the grid. We are at a critical inflection point, and this is a rare opportunity to join the foundational team that will commercialize the world’s first fusion power plants.

In this role, you will apply rigorous analysis to the commercialization of fusion power within the broader context of the evolving U.S. and global electric power sectors. You will develop specialized subject matter expertise on critical drivers of the urgent transition to fusion energy—including commercial deal structuring, scaling a new technology, and how our fusion technology integrates into future energy markets. Working alongside world-class leaders in the premier private fusion enterprise, you will gain unmatched visibility into the commercial mechanics establishing this new industry.

We are seeking a driven, highly analytical professional who thrives in fast-paced, ambiguous environments. Essential qualities include strong initiative, rapid adaptability, and the capacity to convert raw research into actionable insights that drive business outcomes. You will seamlessly bridge high-level corporate strategy and hands-on execution while managing shifting priorities.

This is a career-launching role for a professional willing to dedicate themselves to the urgent transition to fusion energy.

lists.content:
Operational Analysis:
  • Lead quantitative and qualitative analyses to to support the day-to-day operations of the Commercial Power Business teams
  • Establish governance processes and tracking mechanisms to ensure the team executes efficiently on project timelines
  • Produce high-integrity work with strong attention to detail and limited supervision - deliverables may include memos, talking points, slide decks, excel models, and customer briefing materials
    • Customer-Centric Support:
  • Support customer and partner engagements by preparing tailored briefing materials
  • Participating in stakeholder meetings
  • Help manage early-stage customer onboarding and project development activities
  • Translate complex technical information into clear business implications, risks, decision points, and recommended actions
  • Contribute to a continuously improving stakeholder experience when engaging with CFS
    • Energy Policy, Utility Regulatory, and Energy Market Research:
  • Work with Government Affairs to monitor, analyze, and synthesize regulatory developments, utility tariffs, interconnection processes, and local/federal clean energy policies to identify business implications and support strategic decision-making
  • Conduct market intelligence, competitive assessments, and benchmarking to inform strategic decision-making
  • Work with our Government Affairs teams to support the development of testimony and energy policy documents -  this includes conducting research, networking with subject matter experts, drafting briefing papers, and providing analytical support to ensure our commercial strategy is well-represented in key policy forums and industry initiatives
    • Cross-Functional Collaboration:
  • Partner seamlessly with the existing fusion economics, engineering, marketing and comms, government affairs, and legal teams by gathering required market data, providing operational insights, and ensuring fluid information exchange across the enterprise
    • Scalable Business Systems:
  • Design and optimize scalable business development workflows and implement technology, automation, and AI-enabled solutions to drive operational efficiency and organizational effectiveness
    • Executive Communications:
  • Develop, format, and refine executive-level presentations, proposals, and decision-support materials

• Bachelor’s degree in Business, Finance, Economics, Public Policy, Mathematics, Engineering, or a related discipline
  • 5 years of pre- or post-MBA professional experience in energy markets, business development, financial analysis, consulting, or project financeExceptional project management skills and written/verbal communication skills
  • Proven ability to collaborate effectively in a team environment and engage with individuals at all organizational levels
  • Ability to effectively communicate complex ideas in English, both verbally and in writing
  • Strong capabilities in regulatory research, data synthesis, and operational reporting
  • Advanced proficiency in MS Excel and MS PowerPoint (executive presentations)
  • Exceptional problem-solving abilities

• Master of Business Administration (MBA) or equivalent advanced degree
  • Experience in state public utility commission filings, PMP certification, proficiency with project scheduling software (MS Project, Primavera P6), and GIS applications
  • Experience within the clean energy transition, independent power generation, electric utilities, or working with large corporate energy buyers
  • Familiarity with wholesale power markets (e.g., ISOs/RTOs), power generation economics, or energy transition technologies
  • Demonstrated project management experience, including planning, execution, risk management, and measurable business impact
  • Familiarity with data visualization tools (e.g., Power BI), project management software, or CRM platforms

• Perform activities such as typing, standing, and sitting, for extended periods of time
  • Willingness to occasionally travel or work required nights/weekends/on-call - this position will require up to 10% travel
  • Work in a facility that contains industrial hazards including heat, cold, noise, fumes, strong magnets, lead (Pb), high voltage, high current, pressure systems, and cryogenics

lists.content:
• Shape R2R System Architecture: Serve as the chief architect for next-generation roll-to-roll equipment, dynamic tension systems, precision accumulators, and high-speed winders/unwinders
  • Research Advanced Winding & Unwinding Technologies: Actively research, evaluate, and benchmark next-generation web handling, winding, and unwinding equipment and technologies to inform tool architecture and roadmap decisions
  • Lead Cross-Functional Strategy: Translate complex scientific R&D objectives into actionable engineering architectures, bridging mechanical design, process physics, electrical hardware, and closed-loop controls across multiple project groups
  • Master Web Dynamics & Technical Risk: Drive advanced dynamic modeling, web physics analysis, and experimental validation to resolve critical web defects (e.g., thermal buckling, lateral drift, scratching, or tension transients) in flexible metal substrates
  • Establish Division Standards: Institutionalize company-wide engineering standards, design guidelines, and testing methodologies for web handling, precision roller design, bearing selection, and mechatronics
  • Drive Process & Tool Innovation: Pioneer novel mechanical concepts, dynamic guiding schemes, and non-contact web transport modules operating inside temperature zones
  • Independently Manage Risk: Identify, evaluate, and mitigate high-impact technical risks across major equipment initiatives, establishing contingency paths and robust design margins
  • Direct Strategic Vendor Partnerships: Audit, qualify, and direct global suppliers and contract manufacturers for specialized R2R sub-assemblies, precision ground rollers, custom surface coatings, and drive components
  • Organization-Wide Mentorship: Actively coach and mentor Staff, Senior, and Junior mechanical engineers, elevating technical rigor, design review standards, and professional development across the discipline.

• Education: Master’s or PhD in Mechanical Engineering, Mechatronics, or a related field (or equivalent specialized industrial experience)
  • Experience:15+ years of proven track record as a recognized technical leader in the architectural design, scaling, and implementation of complex web handling, roll-to-roll (R2R), or converting equipment
  • Deep Domain Expertise: Authoritative knowledge of web handling physics—closed-loop tension control, winder dynamics, lateral guiding, roller traction, nip mechanics, load cell integration, and substrate stress distribution
  • Cross-Disciplinary Mastery: Demonstrated capability to integrate mechanical systems seamlessly with advanced motion controls, power electronics, and thermal management systems
  • Proven Track Record in High-Stakes Tooling: Successful history of bringing first-of-a-kind continuous processing capital equipment from concept through commissioning and high-yield operational scale
  • Influential Leadership: Demonstrated ability to drive technical consensus and lead multi-disciplinary teams without relying on formal line management authority

• CAD & Simulation Leadership: Advanced mastery of 3D CAD platforms (SolidWorks and/or NX) paired with expertise in multi-body dynamics, non-linear FEA, and finite-difference web simulations
  • Brittle & High-Strength Substrate Transport: Specialized experience handling narrow metal tapes, high-strength alloys, or delicate multi-layer composite webs
  • Advanced Motion & Control Loops: Deep familiarity with tuning multi-axis servo drives, dancer control algorithms, and adaptive tension loops

• Ability to occasionally lift up to 50 lbs
  • Perform activities such as stooping, climbing, standing, or sitting for extended periods of time
  • Dedication to safety to mitigate industrial hazards that may include heat, cold, noise, fumes, strong magnets, lead (Pb), high voltage, and cryogenics

lists.content:
• Shape System Architecture: Play a critical role in the end-to-end design and integration strategy for RF plants for tokamaks, collaborating with other senior engineers to ensure seamless interaction between RF sources, matching networks, and the dynamic plasma load
  • Guide Solid-State & Electronics Integration: Act as a key driver in the architecture and design of the electronics ecosystems required to integrate massive, distributed RF systems, with a heavy emphasis on solid-state amplifier technology and associated power supplies
  • Spearhead Instrumentation & Control (I&C): Take the initiative in designing and integrating advanced RF signal detection, measurement circuits, and embedded digital controllers that interface seamlessly with SPARC’s central data collection systems
  • Tame High-Power Delivery: Serve as a central figure in the hands-on design, integration, and optimization of critical high-power transmission components, specifically large-diameter coax lines and dynamic impedance matching networks
  • Hands-on Technical Mentorship: Act as a senior technical authority on the floor. You will be actively involved in commissioning equipment, troubleshooting the most complex system-level hardware discrepancies, and organically mentoring junior engineers to elevate the entire RF team's capabilities

• Education: Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Physics, or a related field (Master’s or Ph.D. strongly preferred for this level)
  • Experience: 15+ years of hands-on experience in high-power RF systems, radar, particle accelerators, or heavy industrial power electronics
  • RF Fundamentals Expertise: Proven intuition for high-power RF environments, specifically hands-on experience measuring forward and reflected RF power, diagnosing RF arcs, and designing the timing and electronics to mitigate them
  • Electronics & Design: Exceptional skills in RF circuit and electronics design (Altium or similar) specifically geared toward instrumentation, sensing, control, and system integration. Experience in EMI/EMC mitigation to ensure sensitive timing and RF detection circuits operate reliably within extreme high-power, high-noise environments
  • Advanced Simulation: High proficiency in RF/Microwave simulation software (CST, HFSS, etc.) to validate architectural decisions before physical integration
  • Cross-Disciplinary Fluency: A strong systems-level understanding of modern high-performance embedded digital controllers, high speed communications, and fundamentals of mechanical/thermal design to interface effectively with cross-functional teams

• Perform activities such as stooping, climbing, typing, standing, or sitting for extended periods of time
  • Willingness to travel or work required nights/weekends/on-call occasionally
  • Work in a facility that contains industrial hazards including heat, cold, noise, fumes, strong magnets, lead (Pb), high voltage, high current, pressure systems, and cryogenics

Join the power movement as a Principal Scientist - Radio Frequency Plasma Heating
CFS is looking for an enthusiastic experimental RF Scientist/Engineer to join the team to operate the SPARC ion cyclotron heating system and study RF physics/engineering in SPARC and ARC.
The SPARC tokamak aims to be the first magnetic confinement device to achieve net energy and is predicted to have up to Q=11 in DT, producing up to 140 MW of fusion power. The sole auxiliary heating for SPARC is a 120 MHz, 25 MW (coupled) Ion Cyclotron Resonance Heating (ICRH) system that will launch into SPARC via an array of 14 4-strap ICRH antennas. The novel, solid-state 120 MHz sources and the ICRH antennas are already in production.
The Ion Cyclotron Discharge Cleaning (ICDC) System provides one of several mechanisms to clean and condition the exposed surfaces within the Tokamak confinement vessel, including boronization of plasma facing components. The ICDC System is similar in design but wholly distinct from the ICRF, with its own transmitter, transmission network, and antennas.
 The Scientist – Radio Frequency Plasma Heating will be vital to the successful commissioning and operation of both the ICRH and ICDC systems. They will prepare for commissioning via simulations of the antennas and the plasmas and then will be a key part of the team to operate SPARC and to design ARC.

The sole auxiliary heating for SPARC is a 120 MHz, 25 MW (coupled) Ion Cyclotron Resonance Heating (ICRH) system that will launch into SPARC via an array of 14 4-strap ICRH antennas. The novel, solid-state 120 MHz sources and the ICRH antennas are already in production.
The Ion Cyclotron Discharge Cleaning (ICDC) System provides one of several mechanisms to clean and condition the exposed surfaces within the Tokamak confinement vessel, including boronization of plasma facing components. The ICDC System is similar in design but wholly distinct from the ICRF, with its own transmitter, transmission network, and antennas.
 The Scientist – Radio Frequency Plasma Heating will be vital to the successful commissioning and operation of both the ICRH and ICDC systems. They will prepare for commissioning via simulations of the antennas and the plasmas and then will be a key part of the team to operate SPARC and to design ARC.

Commonwealth Fusion Systems is on a mission to deliver the urgent transition to fusion energy.
 
Combining decades of research, top talent, and new technologies, we’re designing and building commercially viable fusion power plants. And we're working with policymakers, suppliers, and many others to build the energy industry of the future.

If that’s you and this role fits, we want to hear from you.


Join the power movement as a Production Technician 
 
The production technician is an integral part of the CFS team performing and monitoring the manufacturing processes required to build and test superconducting magnets. You will have the opportunity to work within a fast-paced, exciting atmosphere to help the team meet the global necessity for clean energy. Ensures functional operation and preventative maintenance of equipment and continuous improvement. Responsibilities include close cooperation with Operations, Maintenance, Quality and other departments to ensure goals and objectives are met. This role will lead the way to making Earth sustainable for the future to come. 
 
This production technician position requires 6+ years' experience in electro mechanical assembly.
 
Hours: 6:00 am - 3:00 pm
Rate of pay: $30 - $41 per hour

lists.content:
• Build a variety of electromechanical parts and assemblies  
  • Work within a multi-disciplinary team to develop and qualify new manufacturing techniques and processes   
  • Perform production builds according to procedures, specifications, and test instructions 
  • Troubleshoot and resolve manufacturing discrepancies with a focus on continuous improvement  
  • Use various mechanical and precision calibrated tools such as torque wrenches, wrenches, allen keys micrometers, and calipers 
  • Read and interpret assembly drawings, wiring diagrams and detailed work instructions
  • Communicate challenges and ideas effectively to peers and leadership
  • Operate production, testing and high-powered magnet equipment
  • Perform other related job duties related to the job, as assigned by management
  • Ability to identify problems in a product and make clear recommendations to better the process
  • Display great attention to detail and a sound understanding of what makes a good product

• High school diploma/equivalency certificate or higher 
  • Minimum of 6 years experience with various hand tools
  • Minimum of 6 years experience in Mechanical or Electrical Assembly

• Experience with winding equipment of any type is a plus
  • PLC Experience 
  • Material processing
  • Working with cryogenic chemicals such as LN2 and Helium in a controlled environment
  • Basic power tools
  • Electrical schematic and wiring
  • Epoxy potting or injection molding experience
  • Plumbing
  • Vacuum systems
  • Soldering
  • Harness builds / Wiring
  • Commitment to safety and quality 
  • Ability to take directions from leadership and work independently 
  • Desire to work and contribute in a fast-paced environment
  • Excellent communication (written and verbal) and teamwork skills 
  • Meticulous attention to detail and cleanliness with hands-on work  
  • Ability and patience to work through projects from start to finish, including assembly and testing
  • Ability to represent the Company in a positive and professional manner at all times

• Ability to occasionally lift up to 50 lbs
  • Perform activities such as stooping, typing, standing, or sitting for extended periods of time
  • Dedication to safety to mitigate industrial hazards that may include heat, cold, noise, fumes, strong magnets, lead (Pb), high voltage, and cryogenicss
  • Willingness to travel or work required nights/weekends/on-call occasionally

lists.content:
• Build a variety of electromechanical parts and assemblies

  • Perform production builds according to procedures, specifications, and test instructions 
  • Troubleshoot and resolve manufacturing discrepancies with a focus on continuous improvement  
  • Use various mechanical and precision calibrated tools such as torque wrenches, wrenches, allen keys micrometers, and calipers 
  • Read and interpret assembly drawings, wiring diagrams and detailed work instructions
  • Communicate challenges and ideas effectively to peers and leadership
  • Operate production, testing and high-powered magnet equipment
  • Perform other related job duties related to the job, as assigned by management
  • Ability to identify problems in a product and make clear recommendations to better the process
  • Display great attention to detail and a sound understanding of what makes a good product

• High school diploma/equivalency certificate or higher 
  • Minimum of 6 years experience with various hand tools
  • Minimum of 6 years experience in Mechanical or Electrical Assembly

• Experience with winding equipment of any type is a plus
  • PLC Experience 
  • Material processing
  • Working with cryogenic chemicals such as LN2 and Helium in a controlled environment
  • Basic power tools
  • Electrical schematic and wiring
  • Epoxy potting or injection molding experience
  • Plumbing
  • Vacuum systems
  • Soldering
  • Harness builds / Wiring
  • Commitment to safety and quality 
  • Ability to take directions from leadership and work independently 
  • Desire to work and contribute in a fast-paced environment
  • Excellent communication (written and verbal) and teamwork skills 
  • Meticulous attention to detail and cleanliness with hands-on work  
  • Ability and patience to work through projects from start to finish, including assembly and testing
  • Ability to represent the Company in a positive and professional manner at all times

• Ability to occasionally lift up to 50 lbs
  • Perform activities such as stooping, typing, standing, or sitting for extended periods of time

  • Willingness to travel or work required nights/weekends/on-call occasionally

lists.content:
• Supervise a team of welders, production, fiberoptic, and composite technicians to build complex electromechanical parts and assemblies
  • Execute production plans, priorities, and schedules established by manufacturing management and planning
  • Partner closely with manufacturing and design engineering teams to resolve build issues, streamline transition from prototype to production
  • Organize daily task lists and workflow by matching production needs with technician skill sets
  • Lead cross-functional daily stand-up meetings focused on safety, quality, cost, and delivery metrics; author and distribute comprehensive daily production updates to leadership and key stakeholders
  • Provide concise, transparent shift handoffs and executive updates to manufacturing leadership
  • Establish and enforce safety protocols (in partnership with EHSS) and maintaining strict workplace cleanliness
  • Design, implement, and manage structured training and qualification programs to build technician competencies across critical manufacturing processes and specialized technical skill sets
  • Manage day-to-day personnel operations, including reviewing and approving timecards, conducting regular performance reviews, and resolving employee 
    relations matters in partnership with Human Resources
  • Lead hands-on R&D and prototype hardware builds with minimal documentation, working directly with engineering to refine procedures
  • Execute production hardware builds and testing strictly following standardized manufacturing instructions, engineering drawings, technical specifications, and quality test documentation
  • Collaborating with cross functional teams, troubleshoot, root-cause, and resolve complex manufacturing discrepancies with a focus on continuous improvement

• High school diploma/equivalency certificate or higher
  • Minimum of 5 years’ experience in a formal leadership role in a manufacturing setting 
  • 8+ years in a technical manufacturing, aerospace, high-tech hardware, or advanced industrial environment
  • Demonstrated ability in reading/understanding technical and electrical drawings, manuals, and reports
  • Experience navigating assemblies in 3D CAD software is a plus 
  • Computer proficiency including, but not limited to, Microsoft Office and Google Suite 
  • Proficiency with ERP/MES systems for scheduling, job tracking, and labor allocation
  • Excellent communication (written and verbal) to your team, articulating in a leadership manner 
  • Meticulous attention to detail and cleanliness with hands-on work

• Formal training or practical experience in Lean Manufacturing, 5S, and Six Sigma 
    principles 
  • Experience navigating complex 3D CAD assemblies (e.g., SolidWorks, CATIA, Creo) 
  • Experience with Precision Measurement & Metrology

• Ability to occasionally lift up to 50 lbs
  • Perform activities such as stooping, typing, standing, or sitting for extended periods of time
  • Dedication to safety to mitigate industrial hazards that may include heat, cold, noise, fumes, strong magnets, lead (Pb), high voltage, and cryogenics
  • Willingness to travel or work required nights/weekends/on-call occasionally

Join the power movement as Project Manager, Project Development

We are at a historic moment, on the cusp of proving the commercial viability of fusion power. This role will play a critical part in taking the next step by managing the permitting process for the world's first grid-scale commercial fusion power plant and laying the groundwork for many subsequent deployments. As the Project Manager, you will support end-to-end siting, regulatory engagements, permitting strategies, and application processes across local, state, and federal levels. Operating within the Project Development team, you will secure vital environmental permits, utility approvals, and land-use authorizations to ensure project milestones are achieved safely, compliantly, and on schedule.

lists.content:
• Perform comprehensive fatal flaw analyses and leverage GIS tools to evaluate potential project locations, assessing topography, generation and water availability, environmental constraints, and overall site viability
  • Working with Government Affairs, evaluate local land-use policies, zoning regulations, and tax structures to determine optimal development strategies and prioritize jurisdictions with supportive regulatory environments for novel energy facilities
  • Support land acquisition negotiations and site control plans, partnering with legal advisors to structure options, land leases, and necessary rights-of-way with municipalities and landowners to achieve positive outcomes for the company
  • Conduct initial real property due diligence tasks, aligning title evaluations, ALTA surveys, Phase I ESAs, and preliminary geotechnical reviews to mitigate risk before formal permitting starts
  • Partner with grid interconnection and power engineering groups to analyze localized transmission availability, sub-station capacity, and grid infrastructure for strategic off-take alignment
  • Collaborate with multi-disciplinary project teams and manage external environmental consulting
    firms and contractors
  • Responsible for overseeing contractor work quality and completeness

    • Early Stakeholder Engagement

  • Lead proactive community outreach during early site identification to establish strong local relationships and resolve potential land-use issues ahead of regulatory filings
  • Represent the company at public hearings, regulatory proceedings, and community forums to communicate project technical details, environmental safeguards, and key benefits 

    • Permitting

  • Lead the strategy, drafting, submission, and execution of major environmental and regulatory permit applications, including Wetlands, Air Quality, NPDES, Storm Water, and CPCN filings.
  • Maintain productive relationships and technical proceedings with federal, state, and local regulatory bodies, public utility commissions, environmental agencies, and zoning authorities
  • Coordinate cross-functionally with engineering, legal, project finance, origination, and external affairs teams to embed permitting requirements into schedules and design basis.
  • Oversee external environmental consultants, legal counsel, and engineering firms in performing environmental impact studies and technical permit preparation
  • Monitor regulatory proceedings, policy updates, and utility dockets to identify risks and implement proactive mitigation strategies
  • Establish and manage post-issuance compliance and turnover systems to ensure adherence to monitoring, reporting, and operational requirements during construction and commissioning
  • Develop and track permitting schedules, establish recovery plans for schedule variances, and maintain the permitting risk registry
  • Build a standardized permitting knowledge base and operational framework to enable multi- site scaling, utilizing AI and advanced digital tools where applicable

• Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering, Urban/Regional Planning, Public Policy, Law, or a related technical field. 
  • 7+ years of experience leading complex environmental permitting, regulatory compliance, or land-use approvals for utility-scale energy, thermal power generation, or large industrial infrastructure projects
  • Technical expertise in federal and state environmental regulatory frameworks (e.g., Clean Water Act, Clean Air Act, NEPA/state equivalents).
  • Exceptional project management skills and written/verbal communication skills

• Master’s degree or advanced technical degree preferred
  • Experience in state public utility commission filings, PMP certification, proficiency with project scheduling software (MS Project, Primavera P6), and GIS applications

• Perform activities such as typing, standing, and sitting, for extended periods of time
  • Willingness to occasionally travel or work required nights/weekends/on-call - this position will require up to 25% travel (day-trip & overnight)
  • Work in a facility that contains industrial hazards including heat, cold, noise, fumes, strong magnets, lead (Pb), high voltage, high current, pressure systems, and cryogenics

Commonwealth Fusion Systems (CFS) is looking for dedicated and highly motivated off-shift Quality Engineers to oversee manufacturing process quality for our HTS Magnet production and the SPARC Project. In this high-impact, hands-on role, you will take ownership of process stability and defect resolution on the production floor, ensuring our manufacturing processes yield reliable, first-of-a-kind hardware. Join the power movement as a Quality Engineer
 
Commonwealth Fusion Systems (CFS) is looking for dedicated and highly motivated off-shift Quality Engineers to oversee manufacturing process quality for our HTS Magnet production and the SPARC Project. In this high-impact, hands-on role, you will take ownership of process stability and defect resolution on the production floor, ensuring our manufacturing processes yield reliable, first-of-a-kind hardware. You will partner closely with Manufacturing and Engineering teams to monitor process health, lead root cause investigations, and manage the end-to-end Non-Conformance Report (NCR) workflow. By implementing robust process controls and risk-informed corrective actions, you will resolve complex fabrication challenges and directly enable the SPARC project mission.

lists.content:
• NCR Management & Defect Resolution:
  • Take ownership of the end-to-end Non-Conformance Report (NCR) workflow on the production floor. Promptly identify deviations, lead material dispositioning, and conduct 8D Root Cause Analyses (RCA) to implement robust Corrective and Preventive Actions (CAPA)
  • Process Plan Execution:
  • Drive process stability by ensuring the successful execution of Quality Plans and detailed Process Plans for HTS Magnet manufacturing and SPARC assemblies. Support the development and maintenance of Control Plans where applicable
  • First-of-a-Kind (FOAK) Quality Monitoring:
  • Monitor process health and hardware quality for low-volume, complex production. Collect and analyze discrete manufacturing data, focusing on defect trending, inspection results, and Measurement System Analysis (MSA) to ensure reliable measurements without relying on high-volume statistical methods
  • On-Shift Quality Execution:
  • Provide technical oversight and leadership for high-priority quality inspections during the off-shift. Execute established measurement and inspection methods to ensure all hardware strictly adheres to engineering requirements
  • Manufacturing Instruction Refinement:
  • Partner closely with Manufacturing and Engineering teams to refine detailed manufacturing instructions and Process Plans. Ensure that quality-critical characteristics are accurately documented, easily understood, and verifiable on the shop floor
  • Supplier Quality Support:
  • Support the supplier quality team by identifying and documenting supplier-related defects discovered during internal production, assisting with root cause data collection and action plans as needed

• BS in Mechanical, Industrial, Material Science or Manufacturing Engineering
  • Minimum 5 years of Engineering experience in a manufacturing, assembly or equipment manufacturing environment
  • 1-2 years of Quality Engineering experience
  • ISO 9001-2015, Six Sigma, Statistical Process Control (SPC), Process Capability Analysis, PFMEA, Measurement System Analysis (MSA), APQP
  • Excellent communication and organization skills

• GD&T and Metrology
  • Knowledge of NDE (non-destructive evaluation) methods including dye penetrant, ultrasonic, computerized tomography, and x-ray
  • Knowledge of cryogenics
  • Minitab or JMP, MS Excel (including VBA), MS Visio
  • Experience with assembly of large metallic components
  • Experience with CMM or Romer Arm
  • Experience with Welding Process and Nondestructive Testing
  • Experience with cryogenic plants, systems, and environments

• Ability to occasionally lift up to 50 lbs
  • Willingness to travel or work required nights/weekends/on-call occasionally
  • Perform activities such as stooping, climbing, typing, standing, or sitting for extended periods of time
  • Work in a facility that contains industrial hazards including heat, cold, noise, fumes, strong magnets, lead (Pb), high voltage, high current, pressure systems, and cryogenics

This engineer will be primarily responsible for testing and retiring risks for CFS’ HTS magnets and in particular, focus on the mechanical, electrical, and process design and construction of the test equipment and supporting subsystems. lists.content:
• Own and retire technical risks by designing, analyzing, procuring, building, and commissioning test equipment utilizing your knowledge of physics, structures, instrumentation and controls, mechanical and electrical systems
  • Understand, challenge and maintain well-documented requirements and risks for the system or component under test
  • Develop test plans that effectively retire technical risks including defining appropriate instrumentation and controls necessary to obtain repeatable and reliable data
    Identify and mitigate safety hazards associated with test equipment and test plans
  • Design safety into the system and produce safety documentation such as job hazard assessments
  • Prepare and lead Test Readiness Reviews (TRRs) prior to executing testing to ensure all test activities are both required and safe
  • Design experiment campaigns that match our fast pace and work hard to maintain the proposed schedule
  • Troubleshoot and resolve integration and test discrepancies during build, commissioning and operation
  • Iterate on designs, equipment and operations for repeat tests to improve test efficiency
  • Create analytical models based on first principles to predict test results
  • Compile test results clearly for review and effectively communicate technical topics to both technical and non technical audiences

• Bachelor's degree in engineering or science field is required; mechanical engineering, electrical engineering or similar applied physics degree
  • 5+ years experience designing/building/commissioning specialized test or industrial equipment with hands on experience and a proven ability to deliver reliable data (A Master’s degree with similar experience may be substituted)
  • 1+ years using CAD software to design electromechanical assemblies
  • Proven understanding of mechanical loading, failure modes, and material strength including fasteners design and bolted joints
  • An understanding of how mechanical engineering fundamentals support complex design maturation including but not limited to tolerancing, GD&T, form/fit/function, material selection, DFM, and DFA
  • A solid grasp of electromagnetic fundamentals – voltage, current, resistance, Ohm’s Law, AC/DC, right-hand rule, solenoids, etc.
  • Proven troubleshooting/problem-solving skills with an ability to innovate creative solutions to challenging problems
  • Proven collaboration skills including active listening and facilitating a productive discourse on problems
  • Exceptional communication skills through both written and verbal methods
    High self-motivation and drive to execute quickly. A can-do attitude and an eagerness to learn

• Experience with structural FEA software, especially ANSYS and COMSOL, bolt loading calculations, and failure criteria
  • Experience using NX and Teamcenter
  • Experience with high field magnet testing traditional or superconducting
  • Experience with weld design / stress analysis
  • Experience with commissioning new test facilities
  • Experience with designing fluid systems – P&IDs, component selection, ASME design codes.
  • Experience with developing and executing complex test procedures, in particular tests that include multiple skill sets, different testing phases, and 3rd parties
  • Familiarity with superconducting magnets (Lorentz loads, magnet design, conductor design)
  • Experience with cryogenic equipment design and use for liquid nitrogen and supercritical helium use – vacuum jacketed equipment, cryocoolers, phase separators, cold traps
  • Experience with high vacuum equipment design and use – roughing pumps, turbopumps, ion gauges, residual gas analyzers
  • Experience with high voltage and high current power equipment design and use – power supplies, water cooled cables, insulation

• Ability to occasionally lift up to 50 lbs
  • Perform activities such as stooping, climbing, typing, standing, or sitting for extended periods of time
  • Dedication to safety to mitigate industrial hazards that may include heat, cold, noise, fumes, strong magnets, lead (Pb), high voltage, and cryogenics
  • Ability to work in industrial or loud environments, with proper PPE
  • Willingness to travel or work required nights/weekends/on-call occasionally
