lists.content:
• Lead and contribute to the design of fluid process systems for testing at varying scales
  • Develop specifications and designs of high-temperature molten salt process equipment, including vessels, tanks, valves, pumps and piping systems
  • Be the technical lead interfacing with suppliers and construction teams to procure, install and commission process equipment
  • At later project stages, support fixed equipment mechanical reliability
  • Support pipe stress evaluations working with piping stress engineers 
  • Collaborate across CFS teams to incorporate R&D learnings and interfacing system requirements into component designs and specifications
  • Actively engage with suppliers, contactors and CFS teams to put safety first at all project stages
  • Track projects and tasks against milestones and report progress up and across the organization

• Bachelors degree in Chemical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or equivalent
  • 8+ years of work experience
  • Detailed knowledge of ASME BPVC and B31.3 and their use in designing process equipment and piping systems
  • Design of industrial scale fixed equipment
  • Design of higher temperature equipment and components
  • Management of external partners and suppliers 
  • Design for hazardous fluid service
  • Experience at a refinery, chemical plant, or heavy industrial facility preferred
  • Familiarity with design/construction codes and standards such as ASME Section I, ASME Section VIII, ASME B31.3, API 510, API 570 AND API 579 preferred
  • Familiarity with P&IDs, CAD, process flow diagrams, analysis such as heat and mass balances
  • Strong commitment to designing for and working in a safety-prioritized environment.
  • Ability to learn new skills/subject matter quickly
  • Ability to work effectively in a multidisciplinary team of engineers, scientists, technical staff and others
  • Ability to clearly express and critique ideas
  • Great communication and organizational skills 
  • Strong problem solving skills, ability to approach new problems with creativity

• Experience with corrosive fluid systems
  • Experience with rotating equipment design, procurement, installation, commissioning and reliability.  
  • Experience with molten salt systems
  • Experience with electro-chemical systems
  • Analysis of pipe stress and support systems
  • Analysis of vessel nozzle loads and stresses
  • CAD software

• Ability to occasionally lift up to 50 lbs
  • Perform activities such as typing, standing or sitting for extended periods of time
  • Willing to occasionally travel to suppliers and support commissioning/test activities
  • Dedication to safety to mitigate industrial hazards that may include heat, cold, noise, fumes, strong magnets, lead (Pb), high voltage, high current, pressure systems, and cryogenics

Now we’re looking for more thinkers, doers, builders, and makers to join us. People who’ll bring new perspectives, solve tough problems, and thrive as part of a team. 
 
If that’s you and this role fits, we want to hear from you.

descriptionBody:
Join the power movement as Senior Metrology Engineer

We’re looking for a Senior Metrology Engineer to join our team to help build robust measurement systems. The Senior Metrology Engineer will be responsible for the selection, development, and upkeep of measurement systems and metrology equipment.  A core skill needed for this role is to be able to develop non-destructive measurements in challenging environments.  The role will interact with R&D technical staff, process engineers and technicians.  This role requires attention to detail, procedural discipline and timely execution. If you enjoy working in a collaborative, fast-paced environment, this is your opportunity to make an impact.

Join the power movement as a Senior Modeling and Simulation Engineer

We’re looking for a Senior Modeling and Simulation Engineer to join our design team to help build next-generation hardware. In this role, you will serve as a lead technical expert for advanced simulations, driving the predictive validation of complex hardware systems.

This role requires a high-level practitioner in multi-physics simulation who can comfortably model complex interactions across thermal, structural, fluid flow, and chemical regimes. If you enjoy solving deeply complex physics problems, applying rigorous modeling standards, and working in a collaborative, fast-paced environment to deliver first-of-a-kind hardware, this is your opportunity to make an impact.

lists.content:
• Execute Simulation and Modeling: Execute advanced Finite Element Analysis (FEA) and Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) for advanced processing equipment
  • Run Multi-Physics Analysis: Build, run, and evaluate highly coupled simulations covering structural mechanics, high-temperature thermal management, fluid/gas flow dynamics, and chemical reaction kinetics
  • Apply Engineering Best Practices: Implement engineering workflows for simulation data management, mesh convergence criteria, and rigorous verification and validation (V&V) protocols using physical test data
  • Drive Design Reviews: Provide analytical leadership during technical design reviews, verifying structural margins, thermal stress distributions, and flow uniformity to guide design choices
  • Collaborate & Interface: Partner closely with cross-functional teams, including Mechanical Designers, Electrical Engineers, Materials Scientists, and Chemical Specialists, to translate simulation insights into actionable hardware modifications
  • Project Accountability: Own and report on modeling milestones, timelines, and computational resources to stakeholders, ensuring on-time and in-spec delivery
  • Get Things Done: Act with speed to solve critical engineering bottlenecks, validating design optimization paths from concept through prototype deployment

• Education: Master’s or PhD degree in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Physics, or a related field with a heavy focus on computational mechanics and multi-physics modeling
  • Experience: 7+ years of experience in simulation and predictive analysis of complex R&D systems
  • Software Mastery: Advanced, hands-on expert in ANSYS, COMSOL Multi-physics, or equivalent high-end FEA/CFD simulation platforms
  • Multi-Disciplinary Analytical Expertise: Proven track record of successfully running coupled simulations (e.g., fluid-structure interaction, thermal-structural behavior, and chemical reaction modeling)
  • Empirical Correlation: Ability to bridge the gap between virtual models and the shop floor by validating simulation results against physical test metrics like strain gauge data, thermal imaging, and flow sensors

• Standards Knowledge: Familiarity with applying industry codes to simulation-driven design validation
  • Motion & Dynamics: Experience running transient dynamic simulations or modeling precision motion systems in extreme thermal environments

• Ability to lift up to 25 lbs occasionally
  • Perform activities such as stooping, climbing, standing, sitting for extended periods of time
  • Willingness to travel or work required nights/weekends/on-call occasionally
  • Dedication to safety to mitigate industrial hazards that may include heat, cold, noise, fumes, strong magnets, lead (Pb), high voltage, high current, pressure systems, and cryogenics

Join the power movement as a Senior Power Electronics Engineer 

Join the Pulsed Electrical Distribution System (PEDS) team at CFS as we begin development on the next-generation power supplies that will power ARC, the first grid-scale commercial fusion power plant. In 2027 our power supplies will supply SPARC with over 1GW of pulsed power. Develop a fusion engineering skillset and learn from SPARC as we demonstrate Q>1. Apply your power electronic experience to develop and qualify   next-generation power supplies for ARC and beyond. We need a skilled power electronic engineer to lead our team.

lists.content:
• Architect and design the next generation of high power (>10MVA) medium voltage power supplies for ARC tokamaks utilizing latest Si and SiC semiconductor devices
  • Collaborate with power semiconductor device manufacturers to develop and qualify new devices for fusion focused applications
  • Model and simulate power electronic circuits and components to evaluate and characterize converter performance, efficiency, stability, etc.
  • Build, test, and validate prototype 4Q power modules (H-bridge, DC link, passives, thermal management, etc.) for use within ARC tokamak power supplies
  • Turn qualified prototype designs into productized solutions for ARC power supplies
  • Develop technical requirements, specifications and qualification plans for corresponding power circuit components (capacitors, magnetics, passives, etc.)
  • Support cross-functional team technical developments such as power distribution, energy storage, RF and other systems delivering electrical power for fusion applications
  • Document designs, simulations and test results into engineering reports

• 8+ years of related experience with Bachelor’s degree (or) a Master’s degree with 6+ years of experience with power electronics based systems
  • Hands on product development experience for power electronic converter systems
  • Knowledge of various inverter circuit topologies and the benefits and limitations
  • Experience with modeling & simulation with analysis tools such as PLECS, PSPICE, MATLAB etc.
  • Extensive experience with semiconductor devices (IGBT, MOSFET, etc.) and magnetic components (transformers, inductors etc.)
  • Fundamental understanding of gate drive circuits, design and device protection
  • Experience with packaging design of power conversion equipment and thermal management
  • Experience with high power electrical equipment >10MVA
  • Experience with hands on testing of electrical components, sub-assemblies and systems in the laboratory and use of oscilloscopes and other measurement equipment
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, ability to conduct design reviews, organize and present results to both expert and non-technical audiences

• Master’s degree in electrical engineering with a focus on Power Electronics
  • Experience with application of compliance standards to the designs (IEC, UL, CSA, NEC etc.)
  • Experience in problem solving, root cause analysis and field containment actions
  • Experience with hands on prototype build, prototype testing and documentation of results is a plus
  • Intelligent gate drive circuit design is a bonus

• Ability to lift up to 50lbs
  • Perform activities such as standing, typing or sitting for extended periods of time
  • Willingness to travel or work required nights/weekends/on-call occasionally
  • Work in a facility that contains industrial hazards including heat, cold, noise, fumes, strong magnets, lead (Pb), high voltage, high current, pressure systems, and cryogenics

Join the power movement as a Senior Process Engineer
CFS is looking for a Senior Process Engineer with deep chemical engineering fundamentals and experience designing, scaling up, commissioning, and operating process systems in large industrial facilities.
 
The ideal candidate comes from an industry such as power generation, petrochemical processing, liquefied natural gas (LNG), industrial gases, chemicals, air separation, cryogenic refrigeration, pulp & paper, or another large-scale process industry. You understand how to translate fundamental process requirements into practical industrial systems and have taken designs from early concepts through Front-End Loading (FEL), detailed engineering, construction, commissioning, start-up, and operation.
 
Fusion power plants bring together process technologies that traditionally span multiple industries. At CFS, you will have the opportunity to work across cryogenic systems including helium and nitrogen, power generation and steam systems, molten salt systems, fueling and gas processing, vacuum systems, and process utilities such as cooling water and instrument air.
 
We are looking for an engineer who understands how these systems behave in the real world because they have personally designed, built, commissioned, operated, or troubleshot industrial process equipment. You should be equally comfortable developing a process design basis, building a heat and material balance, sizing equipment, originating and owning P&IDs, leading a HAZOP, walking down installed piping, supporting start-up, and diagnosing why an operating system is not performing as designed.

Join the power movement as a Senior Process Engineer

CFS is looking for a Senior Process Engineer with deep chemical engineering fundamentals and experience designing, scaling up, commissioning, and operating process systems in large industrial facilities.
 
The ideal candidate comes from an industry such as power generation, petrochemical processing, liquefied natural gas (LNG), industrial gases, chemicals, air separation, cryogenic refrigeration, pulp & paper, or another large-scale process industry. You understand how to translate fundamental process requirements into practical industrial systems and have taken designs from early concepts through Front-End Loading (FEL), detailed engineering, construction, commissioning, start-up, and operation.
 
Fusion power plants bring together process technologies that traditionally span multiple industries. At CFS, you will have the opportunity to work across cryogenic systems including helium and nitrogen, power generation and steam systems, molten salt systems, fueling and gas processing, vacuum systems, and process utilities such as cooling water and instrument air.
 
We are looking for an engineer who understands how these systems behave in the real world because they have personally designed, built, commissioned, operated, or troubleshot industrial process equipment. You should be equally comfortable developing a process design basis, building a heat and material balance, sizing equipment, originating and owning P&IDs, leading a HAZOP, walking down installed piping, supporting start-up, and diagnosing why an operating system is not performing as designed.

lists.content:
• Own process engineering scope for complex systems from early concept through design, construction, commissioning, start-up, and operation
  • Develop process concepts and translate fundamental engineering requirements into practical, commercially viable industrial systems
  • Develop process design bases, operating envelopes, design cases, process flow diagrams (PFDs), heat and material balances, utility balances, P&IDs, equipment lists, line lists, and process datasheets
  • Apply chemical engineering fundamentals including thermodynamics, phase equilibrium, fluid mechanics, heat and mass transfer, transport phenomena, reaction engineering, separations, process dynamics, and process control
  • Develop steady-state and dynamic process models and use engineering analysis to guide system architecture, equipment selection, and operating strategy
  • Size and specify process equipment including pumps, compressors, blowers, heat exchangers, vessels, columns, piping systems, control valves, relief devices, and other unit operations
  • Lead process engineering through Front-End Loading (FEL) and progressively mature systems from conceptual design through process definition and engineering definition
  • Evaluate process alternatives and technical tradeoffs considering performance, safety, reliability, operability, maintainability, capital cost, and lifecycle cost
  • Develop equipment and package specifications, technically evaluate vendor proposals, and work directly with equipment suppliers and fabricators
  • Lead or contribute to process safety activities including HAZOPs, design reviews, relief and depressurization studies, consequence evaluations, and development of safeguards
  • Develop process control philosophies, operating sequences, alarm requirements, permissives, interlocks, and operating limits in collaboration with controls engineers and operators
  • Perform multidisciplinary technical reviews to ensure that systems are safe, operable, maintainable, and capable of achieving their intended process function
  • Support procurement, fabrication, construction, installation, inspection, and field engineering, including field walkdowns and resolution of design and construction issues
  • Develop commissioning plans, test procedures, operating procedures, and start-up strategies and participate directly in commissioning, start-up, performance testing, and operation of process systems
  • Troubleshoot operating equipment and processes using first-principles engineering, process data, field observations, and structured process investigations
  • Capture lessons learned from construction, commissioning, and operation and translate them into improvements in process safety, reliability, operability, maintainability, performance, engineering standards, and future designs
  • Provide technical leadership and mentor less-experienced engineers on complex process engineering problems

• Bachelor’s degree in Chemical Engineering (or closely related discipline)
  • 7+ years of relevant industrial process engineering experience, or equivalent demonstrated depth of experience
  • Strong command of chemical engineering fundamentals including mass and energy balances, thermodynamics, phase equilibrium, fluid mechanics, heat and mass transfer, transport phenomena, unit operations, and process dynamics and control
  • Experience designing process systems for large-scale industrial facilities
  • Demonstrated experience taking process systems through a structured FEL or equivalent stage-gated project development process, from concept and process definition through detailed engineering and execution
  • Experience with process scale-up, technology scale-up, or translating process requirements into commercial-scale equipment and facilities
  • Demonstrated experience developing core process engineering deliverables including process design bases, heat and material balances, PFDs, P&IDs, equipment specifications, datasheets, and process calculations
  • Experience sizing, specifying, and selecting industrial process equipment
  • Hands-on experience operating, commissioning, starting up, performance testing, and troubleshooting industrial process systems and physical equipment
  • Experience working directly with operators and technicians and using operating data and field observations to diagnose process performance
  • Experience with process simulation and analysis tools such as EcoSim, Aspen HYSYS, Aspen Plus, AVEVA Process Simulation, or equivalent
  • Experience with process safety and hazard analysis, including HAZOP or equivalent methodologies
  • Experience with relief system design and overpressure protection
  • Experience working with and integrating other engineering disciplines including mechanical, piping, instrumentation and controls, electrical, safety, operations, and construction
  • Experience working directly with equipment vendors, fabricators, EPC organizations, or construction contractors
  • Familiarity with applicable process industry codes and standards, including ASME B31.3 and ASME BPVC Section VIII

descriptionBody:
Join the power movement as a Senior Process Engineer

CFS is looking for a Senior Process Engineer with deep chemical engineering fundamentals and experience designing, scaling up, commissioning, and operating process systems in large industrial facilities.
 
The ideal candidate comes from an industry such as power generation, petrochemical processing, liquefied natural gas (LNG), industrial gases, chemicals, air separation, cryogenic refrigeration, pulp & paper, or another large-scale process industry. You understand how to translate fundamental process requirements into practical industrial systems and have taken designs from early concepts through Front-End Loading (FEL), detailed engineering, construction, commissioning, start-up, and operation.
 
Fusion power plants bring together process technologies that traditionally span multiple industries. At CFS, you will have the opportunity to work across cryogenic systems including helium and nitrogen, power generation and steam systems, molten salt systems, fueling and gas processing, vacuum systems, and process utilities such as cooling water and instrument air.
 
We are looking for an engineer who understands how these systems behave in the real world because they have personally designed, built, commissioned, operated, or troubleshot industrial process equipment. You should be equally comfortable developing a process design basis, building a heat and material balance, sizing equipment, originating and owning P&IDs, leading a HAZOP, walking down installed piping, supporting start-up, and diagnosing why an operating system is not performing as designed.

lists.content:

  • Collect manufacturing data and conduct statistical analysis using control charts, process capability studies and Measurement System Analysis. Quickly escalate important insights to Operations
  • Support creation of detailed manufacturing instructions to document quality critical characteristics
  • Promptly escalate manufacturing nonconformances and conduct 8D Root Cause Analysis and implement Corrective Actions
  • Play a leading role in developing quality requirements and inspection plans for assembly and commissioning activities, ensuring adherence to engineering requirements
  • Regularly collect, analyze, and interpret manufacturing data, using statistical analysis methods to drive quality improvements
  • Provide oversight on high priority Quality Inspections for the project

• BS in Mechanical, Industrial, Material Science or Manufacturing Engineering
  • Minimum 7 years of Quality Engineering experience in a mechanical assembly or equipment manufacturing environment
  • Experience with GD&T and Metrology

  • Knowledge of GD&T and Metrology and experience with CMM, Creaform, Laser Scanner
     
  • Knowledge of NDE (non-destructive evaluation) methods including dye penetrant, ultrasonic, computerized tomography, and x-ray
     
  • Knowledge of cryogenics
     
  • Minitab or JMP, MS Excel (including VBA), MS Visio
  • Excellent communication and organization skills

• Experience with Welding Process and  Nondestructive Testing
  • Experience with assembly of large metallic components
  • Experience with cryogenic plants, systems, and environments

• Ability to occasionally lift up to 50 lbs
  • Willingness to travel or work required nights/weekends/on-call occasionally
  • May require working long hours occasionally
  • Perform activities such as stooping, climbing, typing, standing, or sitting for extended periods of time

Join the power movement as a Senior R&D Electromagnetic Analysis Engineer
 
The R&D team’s mission at CFS is to vet potential technical solutions in order to guide the overall SPARC subsystem design, and plan for the technology needs of future fusion power plants and spin-off projects.  The Electromagnetics Analysis Engineer within the R&D team will perform electromagnetic (EM) analysis of superconducting magnets using finite element and other methods. This analysis includes the non-linear, anisotropic behavior of high-temperature superconductors (HTS) in both insulated and non-insulated magnet systems. Incorporating complex multi-physics (heat transfer, fluids, mechanics, etc) system behavior into simplified, elegant network circuit and/or FEA models are also crucial to modelling the multi-physics behavior of superconducting magnets. The Electromagnetics Analysis Engineer will also work with a team of experimentalists and engineers to validate simulations against experimental data. Familiarity with both commercial finite element analysis software packages and developing custom in-house code in python and extensions of commercial packages is necessary.
 
This work is conducted within a multi-disciplinary team of physicists and engineers. Participation and clear, concise communication in design and test activities is necessary to both inform design decisions and correlate models to experiment.

Join the power movement as a Senior R&D Engineer
 
The NINT Magnet R&D team is responsible for testing and retiring risks for CFS's NINT (non-insulated-non-twisted) HTS magnets. This includes executing development test campaigns for CFS's next-generation NINT magnet technology, and leading RCCA efforts through analysis and testing to resolve issues that may arise with the SPARC NINT magnets currently in production, tokamak integration, and commissioning. HTS magnet technology is inherently multidisciplinary, and a successful Senior R&D engineer will seamlessly flex between disciplines and groups to effectively lead the execution of tests and projects on aggressive schedules supporting CFS's mission. The Senior R&D engineer must have a fundamental understanding of mechanical, electrical, materials, fluids, and systems engineering, or some combination thereof. Commonwealth Fusion Systems is on a mission to deliver the urgent transition to fusion energy.
 
Combining decades of research, top talent, and new technologies, we’re designing and building commercially viable fusion power plants. And we're working with policymakers, suppliers, and many others to build the energy industry of the future.
 
We’re in the best position to make it happen. Since 2018, we’ve raised $4 billion of capital, making us the largest and leading fusion company in the world.
 
Now we’re looking for more thinkers, doers, builders, and makers to join us. People who’ll bring new perspectives, solve tough problems, and thrive as part of a team. 
 
If that’s you and this role fits, we want to hear from you.

Join the power movement as a Senior R&D Engineer
 
The NINT Magnet R&D team is responsible for testing and retiring risks for CFS's NINT (non-insulated-non-twisted) HTS magnets. This includes executing development test campaigns for CFS's next-generation NINT magnet technology, and leading RCCA efforts through analysis and testing to resolve issues that may arise with the SPARC NINT magnets currently in production, tokamak integration, and commissioning. HTS magnet technology is inherently multidisciplinary, and a successful Senior R&D engineer will seamlessly flex between disciplines and groups to effectively lead the execution of tests and projects on aggressive schedules supporting CFS's mission. The Senior R&D engineer must have a fundamental understanding of mechanical, electrical, materials, fluids, and systems engineering, or some combination thereof. It is also the role of the R&D engineer to constantly push and challenge the requirements, risks, and test objectives that they are given to help the combined stakeholders come to a consensus on why the planned test is required and what data is deemed essential for the outcome to be achieved.

lists.content:
• Develop new HTS magnet designs and their associated subsystems, which includes the designing and building R&D test samples, and developing their manufacturing processes and test operations
  • Design, build, and commission test equipment required to accomplish R&D test campaign objectives
  • Perform structural, electrical, and/or thermal analyses in support of R&D sample design and to predict test results
  • Build expertise in testing HTS magnets as well as how to design and build R&D HTS magnets and their associated subsystems, including power delivery, cryogenic cooling, and structures
  • Support the production, integration, and commissioning of SPARC NINT coils as issues requiring HTS magnet build and test expertise arise
  • Understand, challenge, and maintain well documented requirements and risks for the system or component under test, and align stakeholders on why the planned test is required and what data is deemed essential for the desired outcome to be achieved
  • Collaborate with I&C engineers to develop necessary instrumentation and data acquisition systems
  • Maintain documentation, schedules, and budgets for test campaigns. Documentation includes: design reviews, wiring lists, P&IDs, schematics, CAD assemblies, drawings, BOMs, data acquisition systems, and operations software
  • Develop custom tools to analyze generated data. Compile test results in presentations for review
  • Prepare and deliver presentations containing trade studies, design reviews, test readiness reviews, and test data reviews to teams of engineers and physicists

• Bachelor’s degree in engineering or science field is required; mechanical engineering, electrical engineering or similar, or applied physics degree preferred
  • 7+ years’ experience as an R&D engineer or test engineer designing, building, commissioning complex electromechanical systems
  • Experience working on a multi-disciplinary engineering project, ideally as a technical leader
  • Excellent fundamental knowledge of mechanical systems such as static structures and heat transfer
  • Experience with selecting and utilizing instrumentation and control components such as thermocouples, voltage and current sensors, oscilloscopes, pressure transducers, strain gauges, heaters, flow meters, fittings and valves
  • Experience with developing and executing test procedures
  • Proficiency with CAD design in Siemens NX or equivalent CAD software
  • Familiarity with electromagnetic fundamentals - voltage, current, resistance, Ohm’s law, AC/DC, right-hand rule, solenoids, etc
  • Excellent troubleshooting / problem-solving skills with great attention to detail
  • Experience developing and effectively presenting comprehensive trade studies comparing the pros & cons of various technical approaches
  • Data reduction and analysis skills that can be used in generating anticipated results and processing generated data
  • Effective at communicating technical topics to both technical and non-technical audiences
  • High self-motivation and drive to execute quickly
  • Collaboration skills including active listening and facilitating production discourse on problems
  • Willingness to challenge the status quo in search of better, more efficient methods

• Experience with modeling/analysis software, especially ANSYS, COMSOL, and PLECS
  • Experience writing Python or MATLAB data tools for processing and analyzing data
  • Experience with high voltage and high current power equipment design and use – power supplies, water-cooled cables, insulation
  • Experience debugging electronics hardware and test software
  • Experience with designing and commissioning new test facilities
  • Experience designing fluid systems – P&IDs, component selection, ASME design codes
  • Experience with cryogenic equipment design for use with liquid nitrogen and supercritical helium – vacuum jacketed equipment, cryocoolers, phase separators, cold traps
  • Experience with high vacuum equipment design and use – roughing pumps, turbopumps, ion gauges, residual gas analyzers
  • Experience developing or improving manufacturing processes and handing off processes to production teams

• Ability to occasionally lift up to 50 lbs
  • Perform activities such as typing, climbing, standing, stooping or sitting for extended periods of time
  • Willingness to occasionally travel or work required nights/weekends/on-call
  • Work in a facility that contains industrial hazards including heat, cold, noise, fumes, strong magnets, lead (Pb), high voltage, high current, pressure systems, and cryogenics

Join the power movement as a Senior R&D Technical Project Manager
 
We are seeking a Senior Technical Project Manager (TPM) to join our Project Management Office. This TPM will drive our next-generation High-Temperature Superconducting (HTS) magnet systems. This specialized role requires proven experience delivering first of a kind (FOAK) complex projects from concept to first article prototypes through production ramp up.

lists.content:
• Manage a portfolio of small to mid-sized R&D projects, leading and advising others in project management best practices
  • Frequently act as the primary technical liaison with the executive team, internal engineering teams, and external project management of the scale-up efforts into repeatable sustained operational processes
  • Understand and manage technical tradeoffs between research objectives and operational needs, including but not limited to scalability of the solution, design for manufacturability, material selection, coating technologies, tolerancing, etc.
  • Work with others to ensure your projects are staffed sufficiently with the right skills mix to ensure the projects deliver on their commitments
  • Develop and document comprehensive project plans, outlining project scope, goals, deliverables, resources, and timeline to meet strategic targets
  • Lead a cross-functional team (matrix) composed of engineers, designers, analysts, procurement specialists, and other stakeholders to meet the requirements of the execution plan
  • Foster a collaborative and high-performance team culture to drive project execution and achieve collective goals
  • Monitor project timelines rigorously, identifying potential delays, devising, and implementing mitigation strategies to maintain project schedule
  • Lead the active management of risks throughout the project lifecycle: Identify risks, develop & drive mitigation plans, and keeping stakeholders informed about progress of risks through regular updates & risk reporting

• Bachelor’s or Masters degree in Science, Engineering, or a related field with a PMP or other Project Management certification
  • 10+ years of technical experience, with a minimum of 5 years as a project manager leading new product integration
  • Leader of people in the project management of the scale-up efforts into repeatable operational processes
  • Proven project management experience including scope/requirements definition and management, schedule management and planning, risk management, budget management, stakeholder and communications management
  • Experience acting as a technical liaison with the executive team, internal engineering teams, and external suppliers
  • Demonstrates strong problem-solving skills and the ability to mobilize multi-disciplinary teams to address complex issues
  • Functions as a collaborative team member and a servant leader, maintaining the team focused on objectives
  • Proficient in driving decision-making and execution with available resources
  • Capable of leading strategic ideation and transitioning seamlessly to drive flawless operational execution
  • Possesses excellent communication skills, adapting to various levels of technical proficiency to ensure comprehensive understanding among all stakeholders

• PMP or equivalent Project Management certification.
  • Proven experience managing projects with budgets exceeding $10M and teams of 15+ matrixed personnel
  • Demonstrable expertise in development, fabrication, and testing large, complex prototypes or processes
  • Familiarity with risks and challenges of any fusion power technologies (e.g cryogenics, vacuum, high current electrical systems, molten salts)

• Perform activities such as typing, stooping, standing, or sitting for extended periods of time
  • Willingness to travel or work required nights/weekends/on-call occasionally
  • Work in a facility that contains industrial hazards including heat, cold, noise, fumes, strong magnets, lead (Pb), high voltage, high current, pressure systems, and cryogenics

Join the power movement as an Senior R&D Test Engineer
The role of an Senior R&D Test Engineer is to develop novel fluid systems for R&D test stands, with a major focus on supporting magnet testing. The range of process fluids is broad (liquid, gaseous, cryogenic, supercritical, molten salt, etc.), requiring strong mechanical and chemical engineering fundamentals. The ideal candidate will be resourceful—combining industry best practices, off-the-shelf and customized hardware, and creativity to deliver these fluid systems on tight timelines.
Projects will be on varying scales, from smaller-scale test stands and deep system analysis to larger, complex projects as needed for SPARC and ARC. In addition to designing and building, the engineer will actively operate as a test engineer to commission systems and design automation alongside a team of test/software engineers and operators. You must work collaboratively across production, R&D, procurement, and the SPARC team. Various projects will also require flexing outside of traditional fluids engineering into other disciplines, such as structures and materials engineering, to successfully retire risks for SPARC and ARC.

The role of an Senior R&D Test Engineer is to develop novel fluid systems for R&D test stands, with a major focus on supporting magnet testing. The range of process fluids is broad (liquid, gaseous, cryogenic, supercritical, molten salt, etc.), requiring strong mechanical and chemical engineering fundamentals. The ideal candidate will be resourceful—combining industry best practices, off-the-shelf and customized hardware, and creativity to deliver these fluid systems on tight timelines.

Projects will be on varying scales, from smaller-scale test stands and deep system analysis to larger, complex projects as needed for SPARC and ARC. You must work collaboratively across production, R&D, procurement, and the SPARC team. Various projects will also require flexing outside of traditional fluids engineering into other disciplines, such as structures and materials engineering, to successfully retire risks for SPARC and ARC.

lists.content:
• Design fluid systems for test stands that meet test objectives/requirements, soliciting feedback from interfacing teams as necessary
  • Challenge requirements as necessary to achieve simplicity in design and develop efficient de-risking strategies and plans
  • Perform hand calculations and system level analyses demonstrating sufficient margin for fluid system requirements; build and run Ansys structural and thermal simulations on components and assemblies
  • Procure off-the-shelf process fluid components, manage relationships with vendors, draft specifications for speciality parts and design custom fluid system components as needed
  • Manage the build and commissioning of fluid systems, coordinating engineers and technicians to safely bring systems to operational status
  • Design system instrumentation and automation for safe operations

• Bachelor’s degree in mechanical, chemical, process engineering, or a closely related field
  • 7+ years of experience in the engineering of integrated fluid/mechanical systems (experience with both small-scale rapid R&D and large-scale systems is highly desired)
  • Full-lifecycle fluid systems:
    • Hands-on experience executing the entire lifecycle of large-scale thermofluid systems
    • Component expertise:
      • Experience developing specifications, sizing and working with tanks, process piping, pumps, valves, compressors, purification stages, circulators, heat exchangers, etc.
      • Design documentation:
        • Strong background in establishing system requirements, generating process flow diagrams (PFDs), and developing piping and instrumentation diagrams (P&IDs)
        • Instrumentation:
          • Experience in the design, integration, and troubleshooting of system instrumentation
          • Software and analysis tools:
            • Experience utilizing engineering tools such as ANSYS, COMSOL, 1D compressible flow codes, Python and MATLAB
            • Extreme environments:
              • Practical experience designing, building, and commissioning fluid systems for specialized pressurized, cryogenic, vacuum, and/or elevated-temperature applications
              • Vendor relations:
                • Experience sourcing complex components, drafting technical specifications, and managing relationships with specialized vendors and suppliers
                • Cross-functional communication:
                  • Strong ability to distill complex fluid system details and effectively communicate to non-experts and interfacing teams across R&D, production, and procurement
                  • Problem solving:
                  • Highly driven to challenge assumptions, make efficient technical decisions, and develop innovative solutions on tight timelines

• Adaptability:
    • Ability to flex into adjacent engineering disciplines, such as structures or materials, when required to help retire risks for SPARC and ARC
    • Process optimization:
      • Strong aptitude for identifying bottlenecks and improving throughput during system designs, builds, and commissioning operations

• Ability to occasionally lift up to 50 lbs
  • Perform activities such as stooping, climbing, typing, standing, or sitting for extended periods of time
  • Dedication to safety to mitigate industrial hazards that may include heat, cold, noise, fumes, strong magnets, lead (Pb), high voltage, and cryogenics
  • Willingness to travel or work required nights/weekends/on-call occasionally

Join the power movement as a Senior RF Test Engineer

SPARC sustains fusion reactions by feeding >25MW of 120MHz RF power into the tokamak to heat the plasma to 100 million Kelvin. We need an RF Test Engineer to play a pivotal role in validating and testing the electronics and control systems that power the most ambitious RF plant in the world.

At this level, you are a hands-on executor and technical problem solver. You will be directly responsible for taking newly architected RF and power electronics from the benchtop to full-scale operation. Your day-to-day will span board-level bring-up, operating high-power RF transmitters, and integrating hardware with software controls to ensure SPARC achieves net energy.

For more information on the SPARC RF plant, see the SPARC journal papers here:

  • Overview of the SPARC tokamak
  • Physics basis for the ICRF system of the SPARC tokamak

lists.content:
• Execute Board-Level Bring-Up: Lead the initial power-on, debugging, and validation of custom printed circuit board assemblies (PCBAs), embedded digital controllers, and low-level electronics, focusing heavily on the integration of these boards into working modular solid-state RF systems
  • Operate RF Transmitters & High Voltage Systems: Safely run and test high-power RF transmitters with a primary focus on validating and troubleshooting complex RF behaviors. You will also safely interface with, and occasionally troubleshoot, the supporting high-voltage infrastructure and large-scale supercapacitor banks
  • Drive Hardware/Software Integration: Bridge the gap between physical electronics and control software, ensuring that measurement circuits, timing systems, and sensors interface seamlessly with SPARC’s central data collection and control networks
  • Oversee FAT Fixturing & Operation: Design, assemble, and manage the fixturing for Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT). You will oversee the execution of these tests to validate that incoming hardware meets stringent performance and safety criteria
  • Develop Procedures & Hand-Off: Translate complex engineering validation steps into clear, repeatable test procedures, ultimately training and handing off routine testing and steady-state operations to engineering technicians

• Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Physics, or a related field
  • 7+ years of hands-on experience testing high-power RF systems, radar, particle accelerators, electric vehicles, or heavy industrial power electronics
  • Proven hands-on experience safely working with high voltage components, energy storage (e.g., supercapacitors), and troubleshooting complex analog and digital circuits at the component level
  • Exceptional skills in reading RF circuit designs (Altium or similar) and setting up automated test environments to validate sensitive timing and RF detection circuits within extreme high-power, high-noise environments (EMI/EMC mitigation)
  • Proficiency in C++ and Python, with the ability to read code and thoroughly understand software deployments before testing them
  • Proven intuition for high-power RF environments

• Experience designing test fixtures, writing comprehensive FAT protocols, and setting up automated data acquisition systems in high-noise environments, utilizing EMI/EMC mitigation techniques to ensure circuits operate reliably
  • Hands-on experience measuring forward and reflected RF power, diagnosing RF arcs, and validating the timing and electronics designed to mitigate them
  • Proven experience writing custom test software to automate lab equipment and validate system functionality
  • A strong systems-level understanding of modern high-performance embedded digital controllers, high-speed communications, and fundamentals of mechanical/thermal design to safely execute tests and interface effectively with cross-functional teams

• Ability to lift up to 50lbs
  • Perform activities such as stooping, climbing, standing, typing or sitting for extended periods of time
  • Willingness to travel or work required nights/weekends/on-call occasionally
  • Work in a facility that contains industrial hazards including heat, cold, noise, fumes, strong magnets, lead (Pb), high voltage, high current, pressure systems, and cryogenics

A high-agency, operational leader who bridges external partners and funding agencies with internal R&D, legal, and financial teams, to drive program execution.  In this role, you will take ownership of the federal award program lifecycle after technical scoping. This includes preparing submission documents, leading contract negotiations (Statements of Work, terms and conditions, sub-award structures, and amendments), establishing operational governance, managing high-level schedules in coordination with the R&D Program Leads and Technical Program Managers, coordinating project accounting with Finance, and delivering flawless program execution from contract execution to final closeout.

lists.content:
Lead Contract & Agreement Negotiations:

  • Take direct ownership of contract negotiations for key government-funded programs
  • Work with CFS’ Legal, Procurement, and Global Affairs teams to draft, negotiate, and finalize Government Agreements, Statements of Work (SOWs), required contractual plans, sub-awards, and collaborator contracts

    • Drive Flawless Program Execution & Schedule Discipline:

    • Own the end-to-end operational execution of complex multi-partner programs
    • Maintain master schedules, establish critical-path program management milestones, track progress against commitments, and resolve operational friction before it impacts timelines

      • Manage Contractual Change Control & Compliance:

      • Coordinate with Legal and R&D teams to process post-award scope adjustments, Statement of Work (SOW) amendments, budget realignments, and performance modifications
      • Translate federal (FAR/DEAR) and institutional compliance requirements into clear operational guidance and processes for execution teams

        • Partner with Finance on Budget & Sub-Recipient Operations:

        • Collaborate closely with Project Accounting to monitor program burn rates, track company cost-share/matching funds, review and approve sub-recipient invoices, and prepare audit-ready documentation for financial reviews

          • Unite Cross-Functional Leads & External Partners:

          • Act as the operational nexus for federally funded programs, connecting R&D Technical PMs, Legal, Finance, Supply Chain, and external program officers (e.g., DOE, National Labs, Universities)
          • Facilitate seamless handoffs from technical scoping to formal contract execution

            • Lead Partner Communication & Executive Governance:

            • Organize executive progress updates and site visits as required for successful execution of federally funded programs
            • Produce clear, actionable reporting dashboards for CFS leadership and external sponsors and partners

Required Education & Experience:
  • Bachelor’s degree in Business, Engineering, Public Administration, Law/Contracts, or a related field
  • At least 7+ years of experience leading program execution and contract negotiations for complex, multi-stakeholder technical programs ($10M+/year)
  • Proven track record negotiating SOWs, university sub-awards, or government grants/contracts with clear ownership of contract execution
  • Demonstrated experience coordinating project accounting, milestone tracking, and cross-functional teams (Legal, Finance, Engineering, R&D

    • Flawless Execution Leader:

    • You bring rigorous program management discipline
    • You manage multi-million-dollar programs with precision, tracking milestones, identifying critical-path bottlenecks, and implementing immediate risk mitigation strategies

      • Technically Capable Business Operator:

      • While you do not need to generate deep physics or engineering models, you possess strong technical literacy
      • You can read complex technical SOWs, understand engineering deliverables, and translate them into enforceable contract milestones       

        • Contract & Agreement Negotiator:

        •  You have proven experience negotiating complex technical agreements, Statements of Work (SOWs), sub-awards, and contract amendments with universities, national labs, government sponsors, or corporate partners
        •  You know how to align legal terms, business objectives, and execution

          • Cross-Functional Translator & Information Architect:

          • You excel at translating intricate technical advancements into polished, executive-ready updates
          • Working alongside R&D leads, you synthesize deep scientific milestones into clear progress dashboards, high-impact decks, and audit-ready reporting for government sponsors and external governance bodies

            • Self-Starting Dynamo & Problem Solver:

            • You possess relentless agency and drive
            • You proactively eliminate organizational friction, resolve partner ambiguities, and drive alignment across cross-functional teams without waiting for direction

              • Mastery of Governance & Details:

              • You are obsessive about contract compliance, milestone verification, budget reconciliation, and audit readiness
              • You ensure no detail falls through the cracks

• Master of Business Administration (MBA, MS, or JD) or equivalent advanced degree
  • Experience in deep-tech, energy, advanced manufacturing, aerospace or microelectronics environments
  • Familiarity with federal grant compliance (FAR/DEAR, DOE/ARPA-E post-award execution)
  • Proficiency in project management tools (Jira, Confluence, MS Project)

• Perform activities such as typing, standing, and sitting, for extended periods of time
  • Willingness to occasionally travel or work required nights/weekends/on-call - this position requires occasional travel for partner meetings, government site visits, and industry reviews
  • Work in a facility that contains industrial hazards including heat, cold, noise, fumes, strong magnets, lead (Pb), high voltage, high current, pressure systems, and cryogenics

About Commonwealth Fusion Systems: 
 
Commonwealth Fusion Systems is on a mission to deliver the urgent transition to fusion energy.
 
Combining decades of research, top talent, and new technologies, we’re designing and building commercially viable fusion power plants. And we're working with policymakers, suppliers, and many others to build the energy industry of the future.
 
We’re in the best position to make it happen. Since 2018, we’ve raised $4 billion of capital, making us the largest and leading fusion company in the world.
 
Now we’re looking for more thinkers, doers, builders, and makers to join us. People who’ll bring new perspectives, solve tough problems, and thrive as part of a team. 
 
If that’s you and this role fits, we want to hear from you.


Join the power movement as a Senior Technical Project Manager
We are seeking an exceptional and results-driven Senior Technical Project Manager (TPM) to join our Program Management Office (PMO). The TPM will play a key role in driving complex engineering projects within SPARC, our first-of-a-kind compact fusion machine. The TPM will be responsible for establishing and maintaining comprehensive plans around the engineering, design, procurement, and construction of highly engineered systems and ensuring the team executes to meet the requirements of those plans. The primary focus of this role will be driving Non-HTS projects to closure, with additional responsibility for providing TPM support to critical-path activities within Assembly, including both PASY (Pre Assembly) and SASY (SPARC Assembly).

Join the power movement as a Senior Technical Project Manager

We are seeking an exceptional and results-driven Senior Technical Project Manager (TPM) to join our Program Management Office (PMO). The TPM will play a key role in driving complex engineering projects within SPARC, our first-of-a-kind compact fusion machine. The TPM will be responsible for establishing and maintaining comprehensive plans around the engineering, design, procurement, and construction of highly engineered systems and ensuring the team executes to meet the requirements of those plans. The primary focus of this role will be driving Non-HTS projects to closure, with additional responsibility for providing TPM support to critical-path activities within Assembly, including both PASY (Pre Assembly) and SASY (SPARC Assembly).

lists.content:
• Drive projects within SPARC from inception to completion
  • Develop comprehensive plans for the engineering, procurement, and construction of highly engineered process systems
  • Manage SPARC systems through final design, working with a cross-functional team of engineers, scientists, designers, analysts, and other stakeholders
  • Establish project milestones and ensure all deliverables are met while adhering to strict budget and timeline parameters
  • Develop comprehensive project plans, outlining project scope, goals, deliverables, resources, and timelines to meet strategic targets
  • Support resolution of schedule conflicts and actively drive recovery plans when projects fall behind schedule
  • Track and report SPARC project progress, ensuring project schedules and status accurately reflect execution
  • Facilitate collaboration between the PMO, system leads, and other SPARC project team members to create more efficient project methods, communication, standards, and reporting channels
  • Support implementation of strategic process improvement initiatives and identify opportunities to improve project execution, efficiency, and communication
  • Lead cross-functional teams composed of engineers, designers, analysts, procurement specialists, manufacturing, construction, and other stakeholders to meet project execution requirements
  • Foster a collaborative and high-performance team culture to drive project execution and achieve collective goals
  • Manage cost and schedule while driving critical risk-based decisions throughout the project lifecycle
  • Monitor project timelines rigorously, identifying potential delays, developing mitigation strategies, and driving actions to maintain the project schedule
  • Maintain detailed project schedules and ensure project data in Jira and other project management tools remains accurate and aligned with actual field execution
  • Keep stakeholders informed about project progress through regular updates, reporting, and presentations to management
  • Lead the active management of risks throughout the project lifecycle: identify risks, develop and drive mitigation plans, and keep stakeholders informed through regular updates and risk reporting

• Minimum of Bachelor’s degree in an engineering field
  • High bias for action and ownership with a proven track record of managing complex engineering projects with strong project management skills, leadership abilities, and an understanding of technical project lifecycles
  • Minimum 7 years of experience in engineering and/or project management working with a wide range of engineering disciplines, including mechanical, electrical, and other areas
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal abilities, with the capacity to engage, influence, and lead stakeholders at all levels
  • Strong understanding of project management, planning, and scheduling methods and techniques
  • Exceptional planning, organizational, and time management skills with strong attention to detail
  • Thorough understanding of the engineering product lifecycle, with experience driving products through phase-gate design reviews such as CDR, PDR, FDR, or equivalent
  • Experience developing and maintaining detailed project schedules and using project management tools such as Jira and Confluence
  • Experience with scheduling tools such as MS Project, P6, or equivalent
  • Ability to quickly understand complex technical systems and effectively work with multidisciplinary engineering teams
  • Demonstrated ability to work effectively in a fast-paced, schedule-driven environment and manage multiple priorities

• Previous work experience in new product introduction/delivery programs for high-tech components or assemblies
  • Experience in manufacturing or construction of highly engineered complex systems
  • Experience working in a startup or other fast-paced, rapidly evolving environment
  • Experience with Lean, continuous improvement, or other process improvement methodologies

• Willingness to travel when required or work required nights/weekends/on-call
  • Perform activities such as typing, stooping, climbing, standing, or sitting for extended periods of time
  • Work in a facility that contains industrial hazards including heat, cold, noise, fumes, strong magnets, lead (Pb), high voltage, high current, pressure systems, and cryogenics

Join the power movement as a Senior Test Planning Engineer - Assembly 

This position is overall responsible for planning, drafting and achieving necessary approval of SPARC Assembly Test Products (test campaigns, plans, instructions, procedures) to accelerate project milestones.

lists.content:
• Transferrable knowledge / skillset to become adept / proficient in all defined specialized test methods from both an engineering and equipment operation perspective – specialized testing includes complexity or hazard introduction for design verification purposes (low voltage, high voltage, high stored energy, etc.)
  • Capability to mobilize entire test methods based on innovative technologies
  • Proficient at technical procedure writing – format clean & concise templates for iteration and version control
  • Adept at project risk analysis to establish trade-offs for test schedule gains without compromising safety and quality
  • Diligence (attention to detail) – thorough analysis of preliminary and final design reviews to identify opportunities / develop strategies for risk buy down via test methods
  • Exemplifies correct behaviors to establish a safety-conscience work environment & self-improving culture / learning organization – evident in test product development
  • Generate test procedures / instructions to ensure understanding of scope and identify & mitigate potential risks within both the engineering and technician teams
  • Incorporate test performance and safety standards into test products - pre-job briefs, procedural place keeping, procedural use and adherence, conservative bias, diligent monitoring of critical parameters, correct data capture, etc.
  • Process and action team feedback following test execution to leverage lessons learned, prevent error recurrence and optimize flow for ease of technician execution when deemed prudent
  • Lead complex troubleshooting actions plans and casual evaluations as a result of test anomalies
  • Develop software proficiency with SPARC Assembly workflow management for all test activities
  • Adhere to the highest standards of safety and ensure that activities taking place are being performed in strict accordance with CFS safety policies and applicable regulatory safety standards
  • Ensure that activities being performed in the field are conducted in accordance with CFS Standards, standards published by regulatory bodies (NFPA, ASME, ASTM, NET, OSHA, NIOSH, etc.) and Industry Best Practices
  • Occasional accommodation of off-normal work hours to support critical test activities

• BS in Engineering or related field
  • 7 Years of equivalent engineering experience
  • Previous testing experience with hazards
  • Previous electrical testing experience (high voltage)
  • High proficiency MS Office, Bluebeam or Acrobat, and 3D modeling programs

• OSHA 10
  • NFPA 70E

• Ability to occasionally lift up to 50 lbs
  • Perform activities such as typing, standing, stooping, climbing or sitting for extended periods of time
  • Required onsite 5 days/week when assembly operations with relevant tools are underway, with possible alternating first or second shift assignment
  • Work in a facility that contains industrial hazards including heat, cold, noise, fumes, strong magnets, lead (Pb), high voltage, high current, pressure systems, and cryogenics

About Commonwealth Fusion Systems: 
 
Commonwealth Fusion Systems is on a mission to deliver the urgent transition to fusion energy.
 
Combining decades of research, top talent, and new technologies, we’re designing and building commercially viable fusion power plants. And we're working with policymakers, suppliers, and many others to build the energy industry of the future.
 
We’re in the best position to make it happen. Since 2018, we’ve raised $4 billion of capital, making us the largest and leading fusion company in the world.
 
Now we’re looking for more thinkers, doers, builders, and makers to join us. People who’ll bring new perspectives, solve tough problems, and thrive as part of a team. 
 
If that’s you and this role fits, we want to hear from you.


Join the power movement as a Shift Operator
 
The Shift Operator will be part of the team responsible for the safe and efficient operation of the SPARC Tokamak and supporting systems. Reporting to the Senior Manager of SPARC Plant Operations, this role is essential to support commissioning, operational readiness, and steady-state operations.
 
Shift Operators will perform both Control Room monitoring and field operations, responding to alarms and abnormal conditions, while ensuring safe operating practices at all times. Operators will receive training on SPARC's major steady state plant systems, including:
 
• Electrical distribution
• Cooling Water
• CompressedAir
• HVAC
• Cryogenics Plant
• Other supporting plant infrastructure
 
Additional responsibilities include:
• Procedure development and revision
• Equipment/system troubleshooting and testing
• Performing Lockout/Tagout
• Supporting commissioning and training activities
 
This position is ideal for individuals with power plant or equivalent complex facility experience, who thrive in dynamics environments, and want to contribute directly to the operation of a first-of-its-kind fusion facility.
 
3rd shift - Hours: 10:00 pm - 6:30 am (hours are subject to slight adjustments of one to two hours)
Rate of pay: $30 - $52 per hour + 15% differential

lists.content:
• Operate, monitor, and maintain plant systems and equipment supporting SPARC operations
  • Troubleshoot systems such as cooling water, compressed air, HVAC, cryogenics, liquid nitrogen, and electrical distribution
  • Safely operate plant equipment under normal and abnormal conditions, both remotely from the control room and locally in the field
  • Perform switching and tagging (LOTO) to support maintenance and commissioning
  • Participate in procedure development, revision, and optimization
  • Support testing and commissioning of plant systems
  • Adhere to human performance and safety standards in all activities

  • 5 years in operations at complex facilities

  • Experience with large cooling water systems
  • Previously qualified Lockout Tagout (LOTO) / Tagging Program

  • Comprehensive understanding of engineering principles and theory of operation of mechanical, electrical, and hydraulic systems associated with facility operations
  • Well-developed analytical and problem-solving skill to permit analysis and evaluation of system problems and the ability to apply knowledge and the use of procedures to the operation
  • Excellent communication skills, both verbal and written
  • Excels in a constantly changing environment
  • Ability to learn new things quickly

• Experience in radiological environments
  • Experience with Cryogenic Systems
  • Bachelors Degree in Engineering or related field
  • Strong background in Human Performance
  • Experience with high voltage electrical systems

• Ability to occasionally lift up to 50 lbs
  • Perform activities such as stooping, climbing, typing, standing, or sitting for extended periods of time

Join the power movement as a Staff Computational Materials Scientist
The Materials and Processing (M&P) Department at CFS supports design engineers, supply chain, and manufacturing by selecting materials, unambiguously defining materials and processing routes, validating and measuring those materials and their properties, and conducting R&D to develop new materials and processes to enable fusion power deployment. M&P at CFS is organized around three primary thrusts: engineering, test and characterization, and development programs. The work is undertaken in support of delivering SPARC, the net energy tokamak under construction in Devens, MA, and ultimately in designing the ARC fusion power plant. These devices pose unique materials challenges including neutron fluxes produced by deuterium-tritium fusion, high heat loads, molten salt coolant systems, complex component topologies, high magnetic fields, and high mechanical loading in cryogenic conditions. 
 To support this mission, the CFS Materials Department is seeking a Computational Materials Scientist with expertise in process-structure-properties relationships, physics informed modeling, and materials in extreme environments. The ideal candidate would have a background in both computational materials simulation methods, and materials science and/or physical chemistry. The responsibilities will include physics-based modeling, synthetic data generation, and first-principles modeling and simulation to support development of CFS materials. They will collaborate with other engineers and subject matter experts to identify highest sensitivity parameters and prioritize experimental work for greatest impact to decreasing uncertainty

lists.content:
• Use and build computational toolsets, workflows, and methods to generate predicted material properties in extreme environments including temperature, radiation, and magnetic field with uncertainty bounds informed by physical mechanisms
  • Identify chemical and microstructural features that strongly impact material performance in extreme environments, and quantify the relationships for use in optimization for engineering application
  • Inform design of experiments for materials in extreme environments, including simultaneous corrosion, stress, and irradiation. As well as magnetic field, electric field, and high temperature
  • In collaboration with design and analysis engineers, develop material design curves methodology capable of determining statistically significant minimum properties for tokamak applications such as low and high cycle fatigue, dielectric breakdown, radiation effects
  • Identify gaps in knowledge and experimental capability which can be filled via simulation or model building
  • Assist in benchmarking and creating metrics for material property variability and sources of variability in manufacturing,fabrication, assembly, and  processes
  • Collaborate with other M&P Engineers to create workflows to enable the appropriate capture, storage, data visualization and analysis of data generated within the materials domain
  • Support writing materials standard specifications
  • Stay current with the evolving technology and modeling techniques

• Materials Science and Engineering, Applied Physics, Applied Mathematics, Physical Chemistry, Computer Science or related field
  • Minimum of 10+ years experience in experimental or computational materials science
  • Experience using computational materials science tools and integrated computational materials engineering (ICME) tools to answer specific scientific or engineering questions across length scales
  • Implementation and/or authorship of codes for calculation and analyses of material properties and microstructures
  • Predictive models for material properties and microstructure evolution in extreme environments
  • Validation of models with experimental data or physical mechanism bounds
  • Understanding process-structure-properties-performance principles and fundamental mechanisms responsible for property changes in extreme environments
  • Understanding of the underlying models that enable materials simulation methods across length scales including; Atomistic, molecular dynamics, density functional theory, Monte Carlo, phase field, crystal plasticity, dislocation dynamics, and computational thermodynamics, finite element
  • Scientific computing, numerical algorithms, FEM, FD, FVM, BEM, eigen/linear/PDE solvers, convex optimization, computational geometry, advanced statistical methods
  • High-performance computing: distributed processing, message parsing interface, gpu acceleration
  • Understanding of the sensitivity to uncertainty in the inputs and outputs of those calculations or models
  • Demonstrated ability to work effectively cross-functionally
  • Excellent organizational skills including prioritization of multiple concurrent projects
  • Ability to break down complex problems into smaller deliverables that add value

• Experience displaying complex quantitative data in a simple, intuitive format and presenting findings clearly and concisely
  • Experience making and justifying decisions in fast paced engineering settings
  • Written and verbal communication with technical teams
  • Taking under-defined problems and driving them to a state of completion
  • Operating in a flexible, service-oriented engineering domain team

• Perform activities such as typing and sitting for extended periods of time
  • Dedication to safety to mitigate industrial hazards that may include heat, cold, noise, fumes, strong magnets, lead (Pb), high voltage, and cryogenics
  • Willingness to travel or work required nights/weekends/on-call occasionally. Travel less than 10%

lists.content:
• Lead Electrical System Architecture: Architect complete power and electrical hardware platforms for complex R&D tools, managing power distribution, low-voltage DC systems, cable harness design, and power conditioning. Implement (ANSI/RIA15.06/OSHA compliant) control reliable safety systems for safeguarding industrial equipment
  • Schematic Design & Drafting: Create, modify, and approve comprehensive electrical schematic packages (one-lines, multi-line, I/O diagrams, panel layouts, cable schedules) in AutoCAD Electrical per NFPA 79, NEC, and UL 508A standards
  • Instrumentation & Sensor Integration: Sizing, specify, and integrate power supplies, circuit protection, VFDs, servo drives, safety relays, and precision sensors (thermocouples, pressure transducers, vacuum gauges, flow meters)
  • Signal Integrity & EMI/EMC Mitigation: Design robust grounding, shielding, and isolation schemes to protect sensitive analog/digital measurement signals in high-power, electrically noisy, and high-magnetic field environments
  • Hardwired & Control Safety Systems: Implement ANSI/RIA 15.06 and OSHA-compliant electrical safety circuits, interlocks, light curtains, and emergency stop systems to protect personnel and high-hazard industrial hardware
  • Hardware Commissioning & I/O Checkout: Lead hands-on electrical testing, ring-out, power-up, and I/O validation on the tool floor using multimeters, oscilloscopes, and basic PLC diagnostics
  • Controls & Software Support: Assist controls engineers in configuring EtherCAT/industrial fieldbuses, verifying drive parameters, and debugging basic PLC code (Structured Text/TwinCAT) or HMI screens during tool bring-up
  • Vendor & Panel Shop Direction: Manage external panel build shops and electrical contractors; specify panel construction details, manage component BOMs, and lead Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT)

• Education: Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering (BSEE) or Mechatronics Engineering required (Master’s preferred)
  • Experience: 10+ years of dedicated electrical engineering experience designing power distribution, electrical cabinets, and hardware architectures for complex industrial or R&D capital equipment
  • Electrical Design Expertise: Expert proficiency with AutoCAD Electrical for full schematic generation, panel layouts, terminal block design, and wire harness documentation

The staff fuel cycle and blanket test engineer will support the Tritium and Blanket program closely on executing its research program with integrated tests, building new capabilities, and leading the integration of highly complex capital plant projects that mature the technology readiness of tritium handling and blanket systems towards our first power plant.  The role requires someone who can work in a fast-paced and highly integrated test environment, leading the planning, coordination, execution, and report-out of testing. This role will work within the CFS fuel cycle and blanket technology group. Collaboration with leaders across the organization and blanket and tritium subject matter experts is expected in order to develop and refine tests.

Join the power movement as a Staff Materials Engineer - Metallurgical Engineering
The Materials Department at CFS supports design engineers, supply chain, and manufacturing by selecting materials, unambiguously defining materials and their properties, validating and measuring those materials and their properties, and conducting R&D to develop new materials and processes to enable fusion power deployment. The work is undertaken in support of delivering SPARC, the net energy tokamak under construction in Devens, MA, and ultimately in designing the ARC fusion power plant. Join the power movement as a Staff Materials Engineer - Metallurgical Engineering

The Materials Department at CFS supports design engineers, supply chain, and manufacturing by selecting materials, unambiguously defining materials and their properties, validating and measuring those materials and their properties, and conducting R&D to develop new materials and processes to enable fusion power deployment. The work is undertaken in support of delivering SPARC, the net energy tokamak under construction in Devens, MA, and ultimately in designing the ARC fusion power plant. These devices pose unique materials challenges including neutron fluxes produced by deuterium-tritium fusion, high heat loads, molten salt coolant systems, complex component topologies, high magnetic fields, and high cryogenic mechanical loads. To support this mission, the CFS Materials Department is seeking a Senior Materials Engineer with expertise in metals and alloys in both R&D and production environments.

lists.content:
• Translate component and system performance requirements and failure modes into verifiable critical material property requirements under manufacturing-relevant conditions, and define appropriate test methods to measure and validate those properties
  • Identify materials and processes that enable the high-volume manufacturing of structures and systems under demanding operating conditions, with a focus on manufacturability, scalability, and cost consciousness
  • Select and interpret applicable international materials standards and specifications, and author materials specifications for fusion-specific applications
  • Serve as a technical lead for materials development projects when commercially available materials do not meet application requirements
  • Collaborate with design, supply chain, and manufacturing engineers to select, approve, and qualify materials and processing methods
  • Provide on-demand subject matter expertise for production root cause analyses and corrective action plans involving raw or as-fabricated materials
  • Review, interpret, and report materials property data in version-controlled databases for engineering use

• Master’s degree with post-graduate experience in metallurgy, materials science, or a related discipline. Depending on experience and qualification, a bachelor’s degree will also be considered
  • Minimum of 10+ years experience
  • Experience with large-scale metal production processes, such as casting, forging, rolling, and drawing, and/or large-scale joining processes, such as soldering
  • Experience collaborating and communicating effectively with technical teams at vendors and suppliers
  • Familiarity with scaling metal and alloy design and development from R&D to full-scale products.
  • Strong understanding of process–structure–properties–performance relationships in materials.
  • Knowledge of materials behavior in cryogenic and high-temperature applications, and the effects of nuclear and plasma environments is a plus
  • Strong problem-solving skills, with the ability to approach new and under-defined problems with creativity.
  • Experience with agile project management and effective task execution
  • Ability to work effectively in a multidisciplinary team of engineers, scientists, technical staff, and other stakeholders
  • Ability to operate effectively within a flexible, service-oriented engineering organization

• Demonstrated success in delivering new alloys or materials processes from design and development through at-scale implementation
  • Experience authoring materials standards and specifications
  • Experience communicating materials design and development approaches, results, and performance metrics to both technical and executive leadership
  • Demonstrated ability to make and justify materials and engineering decisions in fast-paced development and production environments
  • Demonstrated ability to take under-defined problems and drive them to completion

• Perform activities such as typing and sitting for extended periods of time
  • Dedication to safety to mitigate industrial hazards that may include heat, cold, noise, fumes, strong magnets, lead (Pb), high voltage, and cryogenics
  • Willingness to travel or work required nights/weekends/on-call occasionally. Travel less than 10%
